title: Crushing PLO Tournaments Review: Is Dylan Weisman’s Upswing Course Worth $999?
excerpt: If you’ve played a Pot-Limit Omaha tournament in the last two years and felt like you were guessing on every street, you’re not alone. PLO MTT fields have exploded, the prize…
content_html:
If you’ve played a Pot-Limit Omaha tournament in the last two years and felt like you were guessing on every street, you’re not alone. PLO MTT fields have exploded, the prize pools are some of the juiciest in poker, and yet almost every “PLO course” on the market is really a cash game course in disguise.

Crushing PLO Tournaments by Dylan Weisman, released on Upswing Poker on April 20, 2026, is the first training product built from the ground up for PLO tournament play. After working through the curriculum, this review covers what’s actually inside, where the course is strongest, where it falls short, and whether the $999 price tag is justified.

Quick Verdict

Rating: 9.3 / 10

Crushing PLO Tournaments is the most rigorous PLO tournament course on the market and easily the best resource available for anyone serious about beating PLO MTTs. The custom solver work, the limp-and-pot framework, and the depth of ICM coverage are not available anywhere else. It’s expensive, it’s not a beginner course, and you’ll need to put in real reps to extract the value — but if you regularly play PLO tournaments above $100 buy-ins, this pays for itself fast.

Best for: Experienced PLO players, NLHE tournament regs crossing over to PLO, and live tournament grinders. Not for: Complete poker beginners, or players who haven’t yet got the basics of PLO down (try Dylan’s PLO Launch Pad first).

→ Get Crushing PLO Tournaments on Upswing Poker

Who Is Dylan Weisman?

Dylan Weisman (online as “iheartco0kie”) is one of the most accomplished mixed-game and PLO pros currently teaching publicly. His tournament resume includes:

  • 2 WSOP bracelets
  • A $1.66M finish on the Triton Super High Roller Series
  • $6M+ in live tournament earnings
  • Years as a regular in some of the toughest high-stakes PLO games in the world

What sets Dylan apart from most high-stakes pros is that he can actually teach. He has a background in education, and endorsements from peers like Erik Seidel and Brian Rast repeatedly mention the same thing — Dylan has a rare ability to translate dense game theory into heuristics you can use under pressure. That’s something most solver-based courses fail at, and it shows up immediately when you start working through this material.

What’s Inside Crushing PLO Tournaments?

The course contains 20+ hours of video across 8 modules and 50+ lessons, plus hand reviews, play-and-explains, and supporting tools. Here’s the high-level breakdown:

1. Preflop (The Largest Module)

This is the backbone of the course and where Crushing PLO Tournaments departs most sharply from standard PLO content. Instead of recycling raise-or-fold cash ranges, Dylan teaches a limp-and-pot preflop system built on custom MonkerSolver work at every relevant tournament stack depth:

  • 100bb (deep)
  • 35bb (middle stages)
  • 20bb (late-stage / bubble)
  • 10bb (short stack / push-fold equivalent)

If you’ve been carrying NLHE preflop instincts into PLO MTTs, the ranges in this module alone will reshape how you play the first 20 hands of every tournament. The limp-and-pot framework is designed to reduce variance and let you play more hands profitably without bloating pots out of position.

2. Postflop Heuristics

Two sub-modules cover single-raised pots and multiway pots, with frameworks for c-bet sizing, board texture reads, and crucially, reverse implied odds — the biggest leak Hold’em converts bring to four-card poker.

3. ICM (The Standout Section)

This is where the course separates itself from anything else available. Most PLO content waves at ICM and moves on. Dylan dedicates an entire module to preflop and postflop ICM analysis, with sims you genuinely cannot find elsewhere. If you regularly cash deep in PLO MTTs, this module is worth the price of the course on its own. One correctly played pay-jump decision at a $500+ buy-in final table easily pays back the $999 investment.

4. Final Table Dynamics

Stack distribution, middling-stack pressure, and how PLO’s flatter equity distributions change ICM math compared to NLHE.

5. Final Table Reviews & Play-and-Explains

Dylan walks through real hands from his Triton, WSOP, and PGT runs, comparing his in-game decisions to solver outputs. This is the kind of material you used to need private coaching at $500+/hour to access.

The Limp-and-Pot Framework: Why It Matters

The core innovation in Crushing PLO Tournaments is the limp-and-pot preflop strategy. Most PLO players default to a raise-or-fold approach borrowed from cash games, which forces too many marginal hands into 3-bet pots where they get crushed.

In a tournament environment — where there’s no rake, antes increase incentive to see flops, and stack depths vary wildly — limping a structured portion of your range and potting (raising the pot) with another defined portion is provably more profitable than the default raise-or-fold approach used by most tournament regs. Dylan and his analyst Matt Wright spent over 1,000 hours and five years running the sims to back this up.

This isn’t a gimmick. It’s a fundamentally different preflop architecture, and it’s the kind of edge that compounds across thousands of hands.

Bonuses Included

Every purchase comes with three bonuses:

  1. Dylan Coaches Brad Owen — A full coaching session where Dylan walks the popular vlogger through a ClubWPT Gold PLO tournament in real time.
  2. Private Discord Community — Members-only server with strategy groups.
  3. Full Twitch Stream — Uncut footage from one of Dylan’s recent deep final table runs.
  4. PLO Trainer App Access — One month free when the tool fully launches (early buyers get unlimited beta access).

The Discord is more valuable than most “community” bonuses because it’s a small, vetted group of buyers — the signal-to-noise ratio in the strategy channels is genuinely high.

Pros and Cons

Pros

  • Only course built specifically for PLO tournaments, not adapted from cash
  • Custom MonkerSolver work across all relevant stack depths
  • ICM coverage you cannot find anywhere else
  • Real hand reviews from $25K–$75K live final tables
  • Dylan’s teaching style is clear, structured, and theory-light when it counts
  • Lifetime access plus PLO Trainer App
  • Strong endorsements from Erik Seidel, Brian Rast, and other high-stakes legends
  • Covered by Upswing’s Fair Play Satisfaction Guarantee

Cons

  • $999 is steep — this is a serious investment, not an impulse buy
  • Not a beginner course — you need a working PLO foundation already
  • 20+ hours of material requires real study time to internalize
  • Limp-and-pot framework requires unlearning habits, which can hurt short-term results before it helps
  • No free trial (though the satisfaction guarantee covers you)

Who Should Buy Crushing PLO Tournaments?

You should buy this course if you:

  • Regularly play PLO tournaments at $200+ buy-ins online or live
  • Are an NLHE MTT regular looking to add PLO to your game
  • Have completed an intro PLO course (or have logged real volume) and want to take the next step
  • Make deep runs in PLO MTTs and feel like you’re guessing at final tables

You should skip it (for now) if you:

  • Are brand new to PLO — start with Dylan’s PLO Launch Pad instead
  • Only play micro-stakes PLO tournaments where ROI on a $999 course is hard to justify
  • Are primarily a PLO cash game player — Advanced PLO Mastery is a better fit

Is It Worth the $999?

This is where most reviews handwave, so let’s actually do the math.

A single correct ICM decision at a $1,000 buy-in PLO final table can swing $2,000–$5,000+ in equity, depending on stack distribution and payout structure. PLO MTT players who final-table once a year and get even one major decision right that they previously got wrong have already 5x’d their investment.

For a player with any reasonable PLO MTT volume above $200 buy-ins, the course pays for itself the first time you correctly navigate a pay-jump decision you would have previously punted. That’s not marketing copy — it’s just how the math works in tournaments with steep payout curves.

If you exclusively play $20 PLO MTTs on weekends, the ROI calculation looks different, and the cost is harder to justify. Be honest with yourself about your volume and stakes.

Final Verdict

Crushing PLO Tournaments is the new gold standard for PLO tournament training. It’s the first course that treats PLO MTTs as their own discipline rather than a footnote attached to cash game theory, and the depth of solver work and ICM analysis is genuinely unmatched.

The $999 price will keep casual players out, which is probably the point — Dylan clearly wants serious students. If you fit the profile, this is the easiest “yes” in poker training right now.

Rating: 9.3 / 10

→ Get Crushing PLO Tournaments on Upswing Poker

Frequently Asked Questions

How long is Crushing PLO Tournaments?

The course contains 20+ hours of video content across 8 modules and 50+ lessons, plus bonus content including a full coaching session and a real-time tournament stream.

Do I need to know PLO before buying?

Yes. This is an advanced course. If you’re new to PLO, start with Dylan Weisman’s PLO Launch Pad first, then come back to this once you’ve got the basics down.

Is there a money-back guarantee?

The course is covered by Upswing Poker’s Fair Play Satisfaction Guarantee, though there is no traditional free trial. Reach out to their support team if the course isn’t a fit.

How does this compare to Advanced PLO Mastery?

Advanced PLO Mastery (also by Dylan, with Chris Wehner) is focused on PLO cash games. Crushing PLO Tournaments is purpose-built for MTTs and includes ICM, stack-depth-specific preflop ranges, and final table dynamics that aren’t covered in the cash course.

Will the strategy work in low-stakes PLO tournaments?

Absolutely. In fact, soft low-to-mid stakes PLO MTT fields are where the edge is largest — players in those games are making fundamental preflop and ICM mistakes that this course directly addresses.

Disclosure: This review may contain affiliate links. We only recommend products we believe deliver genuine value to our readers.

title: Run It Once vs Upswing Poker: Which Poker Training Site Is Right for You in 2026?
excerpt: If you’ve spent more than ten minutes researching poker training sites, you’ve run into both of them: Run It Once and Upswing Poker. They’re the two biggest names in serious…
content_html:
If you’ve spent more than ten minutes researching poker training sites, you’ve run into both of them: Run It Once and Upswing Poker. They’re the two biggest names in serious No-Limit Hold’em and PLO education, they’re both founded by world-class pros, and they’ve both been refining their offering for over a decade.

But they are not the same product. One is a vast video library you graze across at your own pace. The other is a structured course you work through from start to finish. Picking the wrong one for your situation costs you money, time, and — more importantly — momentum.

This guide breaks down everything that actually matters: pricing, coaches, content depth, learning structure, community, and who each site is genuinely built for.

Quick Verdict

  • Choose Run It Once if you’re an intermediate-to-advanced player who learns by exposure, wants access to the biggest names in high-stakes poker, and plays multiple formats (NLHE, PLO, MTT, mixed games).
  • Choose Upswing Poker if you’re a beginner-to-intermediate player who wants a clear, guided study path with a placement quiz, structured modules, and a defined finish line.

If you only want a single answer: Upswing Lab 2.0 is the better starting point for most players under mid-stakes; Run It Once Elite is the better long-term home for serious grinders aiming at mid-to-high stakes.

Run It Once: The High-Stakes Library

Background

Run It Once was launched in December 2012 by Phil Galfond and his business partner Dan Quinn. Galfond is one of the most respected high-stakes players and instructors in the game, and from the start the platform’s positioning was clear: the “first-class cabin” of poker training.

More than a decade later, that’s still the brand. Run It Once now operates with a roster of over 170 coaches — a who’s who of modern poker that includes Phil Galfond himself, Jason Koon, Justin Bonomo, Dan Smith, Stephen Chidwick, Kevin Rabichow, and many others. Collectively the roster holds more than 40 WSOP bracelets and hundreds of millions in tournament earnings.

Content

This is where Run It Once is in a class of its own. The Elite tier gives access to roughly 9,500+ training videos, with two new videos uploaded every single day — a release cadence the site has maintained, almost without exception, since 2012. The Essential tier is more modest but still substantial, with 3,000+ videos and five new uploads per week.

Coverage is wide. You’ll find content on:

  • No-Limit Hold’em (cash and tournaments)
  • Pot-Limit Omaha (cash and tournaments)
  • Mixed games and less-popular variants
  • Mental game and coaching from specialists like Elliot Roe
  • Heads-up play
  • Stake-specific content from micros up to nosebleeds

Run It Once also bundles in its Vision GTO Trainer for PLO — a visual range trainer that works without a separate solver — plus Learning Paths that curate videos into structured study blocks. New videos ship with translated captions in eight languages, which matters if English isn’t your first language.

Pricing

  • Basic — Free. Three Elite videos, forum and Discord access, video previews.
  • Essential — Around $25/month. Full Essential video library, five new videos weekly.
  • Elite — $199/month or $1,400/year. Everything in Essential plus the full Elite library, two new daily uploads, monthly Q&As with top coaches, private Discord channels, study groups, and monthly seminars.

The Elite tier is a serious commitment. It is priced for players who treat poker as a profession — or are seriously trying to.

Strengths

  • Unmatched coaching roster
  • Enormous, constantly growing library
  • Genuine high-stakes content (most other sites peak at mid-stakes)
  • Multi-format coverage (NLHE, PLO, mixed, MTT)
  • Built-in PLO solver tool (Vision)
  • Long-term home for a study habit — there’s always new content

Weaknesses

  • The sheer volume can paralyze beginners
  • No single “learn poker in order” path — you have to self-direct
  • Elite pricing is steep for low-stakes players
  • Quality varies across 170 coaches

Upswing Poker: The Structured Course

Background

Upswing Poker was founded in 2015 by Doug Polk, Ryan Fee, and Matt Colletta. It grew out of a strategy blog with free preflop charts into one of the largest poker training brands in the world. Doug Polk’s high-profile heads-up matches and YouTube channel made the brand instantly recognizable; the courses are what kept members paying.

In 2026, the flagship product is Lab 2.0, headed by coach Uri Peleg — a high-stakes crusher and founder of the staking firm Guerrilla Poker. The roster also includes Nick Petrangelo (tournaments), Doug Polk (his End Boss System), Gary Blackwood, Dylan Weisman, Jake Abdalla, and Fabian Adler.

Content

Upswing’s approach is fundamentally different from Run It Once. Rather than a sprawling library, Lab 2.0 is a guided course. New members take a placement quiz so they start exactly where their game needs work, and progress through a structured learning path that adapts as they advance. The Lab is built around defined tracks:

  • Online Cash
  • Live Cash
  • Tournaments
  • Mastery Path
  • Max Exploit Academy (exploitative adjustments)
  • Strategy Specials
  • Levels (a recent series by Uri Peleg starting at low stakes and working up)

Outside the Lab, Upswing sells standalone premium courses. The big one is Doug Polk’s End Boss System (a $499+ deep dive into preflop strategy and exploitative adjustments for NL200 and above). Nick Petrangelo has a tournament series. Other courses cover PLO, mixed games, heads-up, and short deck — typically in the $499–$999 range.

The Lab also includes 400+ preflop charts, regular live Q&As, weekly webinars, and a private Discord with coaches actively answering questions.

Pricing

  • Lab 2.0 — $99/month, $399 for 6 months, or $699/year.
  • Standalone courses — One-time payments from $7 (the Postflop Playbook) up to $999 (Mixed Games Mastery).
  • Guarantee — 30-day money-back guarantee for new Lab members. No free trial.

Strengths

  • Clear, structured learning path with a defined start and finish
  • Adaptive placement quiz so beginners don’t waste time on material they know
  • Coaches actively engage in the Discord — questions get answered
  • Premium standalone courses for specific weaknesses
  • 30-day money-back guarantee
  • Strong preflop chart library

Weaknesses

  • Much narrower coaching roster than Run It Once
  • Library is smaller — once you finish the Lab, the well runs shallower
  • Less high-stakes-specific content (Lab caps out around mid-stakes for most players)
  • Premium courses get expensive quickly
  • No free trial — you commit before you see the inside

Head-to-Head Comparison

Which One Wins on… ?

Coaching Roster

Winner: Run It Once. This isn’t close. Run It Once’s roster is the deepest in poker — three of the all-time top-five tournament earners contribute videos. Upswing has top-tier names (Polk, Peleg, Petrangelo) but a fraction of the depth.

Structure for Beginners

Winner: Upswing Poker. Lab 2.0’s placement quiz and adaptive path is the single most beginner-friendly feature in serious poker training. Run It Once has Learning Paths, but you still have to self-direct.

Value for Low-Stakes Players

Winner: Run It Once Essential. At $25/month for 3,000+ videos, it’s the best entry-level deal in poker education. Upswing Lab at $99/month is harder to justify if you’re playing $0.05/$0.10 NLHE.

Value for Mid-to-High Stakes Players

Winner: Run It Once Elite. The Elite tier is the only training subscription on the market that consistently teaches actual high-stakes content from people currently playing it. Upswing’s End Boss System is excellent but narrower in scope.

PLO and Mixed Games

Winner: Run It Once. No serious contest. Run It Once was built on Galfond’s PLO expertise, Vision is a genuinely useful PLO tool, and the mixed-game content is broader. Upswing offers good PLO and mixed game courses, but they’re standalone purchases.

Coach Interaction

Winner: Upswing Poker. Uri Peleg and the Lab 2.0 team are actively engaged in the Discord, answering hand-history questions directly. Run It Once has Q&As, but its scale makes one-on-one interaction rarer.

Community

Tie. Both have active Discord servers and forums. Run It Once’s is larger; Upswing’s is more focused.

Who Should Choose Run It Once

  • You’re playing 50NL or higher (online) or $2/$5 live and above
  • You play multiple formats and want one subscription that covers them all
  • You learn well from watching pros think out loud, even without a strict curriculum
  • You want exposure to the absolute top of the game
  • PLO, MTTs, or mixed games are part of your game
  • You’re committed to a long-term study habit and need a deep well

Who Should Choose Upswing Poker

  • You’re a beginner or intermediate NLHE cash player
  • You want a clear, guided path with milestones
  • Preflop ranges and structured charts matter to you
  • You learn better from a focused course than from browsing a library
  • You want direct access to coaches in a smaller community
  • You’re considering a specific premium course (End Boss, a Petrangelo MTT series, etc.)

Can You Use Both?

Honestly — many serious players do, just not at the same time. A common path:

  1. Start with Upswing Lab 2.0 for six months to build foundations and fix obvious leaks.
  2. Cancel and move to Run It Once Essential or Elite once you’ve outgrown the structured curriculum and need depth, variety, and high-stakes content.
  3. Add specific Upswing premium courses (End Boss, PLO Mastery) when you identify a clear weakness.

This sequence respects how players actually develop: structure first, depth later.

Final Verdict

There’s no objectively “better” site here. There’s only the right site for where you are right now.

Upswing Poker is the better on-ramp. The Lab is the most thoughtfully structured product in poker training, and for a player who needs a roadmap, it pays for itself fast.

Run It Once is the better long-term home. The roster, the library, and the multi-format coverage make it the default destination for players whose goal is to play poker for a living, or at least to take it that seriously.

If you’re playing micro to small stakes and feel lost, start with Upswing. If you’re already a winning small-stakes player aiming higher, go straight to Run It Once. Either way, the bigger leak in your game is probably not which site you pick — it’s how disciplined you are about actually studying.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Run It Once still owned by Phil Galfond? The Run It Once training site is still operated under Galfond’s direction. The separate Run It Once Poker room was integrated into BetRivers Poker some time ago, but the training platform — the subject of this comparison — continues as Galfond’s project.

Does Upswing Poker have a free trial? No free trial, but Lab 2.0 comes with a 30-day money-back guarantee for first-time members.

Which site is better for tournament players? Both are strong here. Run It Once has more tournament coaches at the elite level (Koon, Bonomo, Chidwick, Smith). Upswing has Nick Petrangelo and a focused tournament track inside the Lab. If you play live MTTs at high buy-ins, Run It Once wins. If you’re grinding online MTTs and want a curriculum, Upswing is excellent.

Is the Run It Once Elite tier worth $199/month? For a full-time poker professional or a committed serious amateur playing mid-stakes or higher: yes, easily. For someone playing recreational low-stakes: no — Essential at $25/month gives you 90% of what you actually need.

Can a complete beginner use Run It Once? Yes, especially via the “From the Ground Up” course and Learning Paths. But Upswing Lab 2.0 is genuinely better designed for beginners because of the adaptive placement.

How often is content updated? Run It Once releases two new videos per day on Elite and five per week on Essential. Upswing updates the Lab regularly and adds live Q&As, but doesn’t operate on a daily-release schedule.

Do either offer 1-on-1 coaching? Both offer access to private coaching through their coaches outside the subscriptions, typically arranged directly with individual pros. Neither subscription itself includes scheduled 1-on-1 sessions — though Upswing’s Lab coach interaction in Discord gets close.

Whichever you choose, the same advice applies: build a study routine, review your own hands, and apply what you learn at the tables the same week you study it. The site is the tool — the discipline is the edge.

title: Upswing Lab 2.0 Review: The Most Complete No-Limit Hold’em Training Course in 2026?
excerpt: If you’re serious about improving your poker game, you’ve almost certainly heard of Upswing Poker. Their flagship training product — the Upswing Lab — has been one of the most…
content_html:
If you’re serious about improving your poker game, you’ve almost certainly heard of Upswing Poker. Their flagship training product — the Upswing Lab — has been one of the most talked-about coaching programs in the industry for years. Now, with the launch of Lab 2.0, the platform has been completely rebuilt from the ground up. But is it worth your money? We dug deep to find out.

What Is Upswing Lab 2.0?

Upswing Lab 2.0 is a subscription-based No-Limit Hold’em training membership designed to take players from wherever they currently are and move them steadily toward elite-level play. Taught by high-stakes crusher and world-class poker coach Uri Peleg, the course provides a clear, structured path to poker mastery — whether you’re a beginner or an experienced reg looking to sharpen your edge.

This isn’t just a refresh of the original Lab. Lab 2.0 is built as a smart, adaptive learning path: a placement quiz ensures you begin exactly where you need to, with no retracing of material you’ve already mastered. That alone sets it apart from the one-size-fits-all approach that plagues most poker training sites.

Who Is Uri Peleg?

The head coach behind Lab 2.0 deserves a proper introduction. Uri Peleg is the founder of staking company Guerrilla Poker and a world-class strategist with over $2 million in personal winnings. His students have collectively earned more than $25 million at the tables. Perhaps most impressively, he also holds a Magic: The Gathering World Championship title — a testament to his mastery of complex strategic thinking.

Members consistently praise his ability to simplify complex concepts without ever dumbing them down, noting it’s a rare skill to make things clear while still preserving their depth.

What’s Inside Upswing Lab 2.0?

Structured Learning Path

Lab 2.0 is built around a progressive curriculum that avoids the common trap of dumping hundreds of hours of unorganized content on members. You follow a Launch Pad before entering the more advanced Mastery Path — progressively structured from foundations to elite exploits, with weekly additions including new lessons and Max Exploit Academy content.

Elite Video Training

The core of the course is high-quality video instruction from Uri and a hand-selected team of coaches. Members report that even content on familiar topics can deliver genuine “aha” moments — which is the hallmark of truly exceptional teaching.

Interactive Tools & Quizzes

Unlike passive video courses where you sit and watch, Lab 2.0 includes interactive practice tools and quizzes that let you test your knowledge, receive feedback, and pinpoint your weaknesses.This active learning approach accelerates improvement significantly.

Preflop Prodigy App

One of the standout additions in Lab 2.0, the Preflop Prodigy App lets you master expert preflop ranges on any device, for both cash games and tournaments. This is the kind of tool that turns abstract theory into muscle memory.

Live Coaching & Weekly Q&As

Members get access to weekly Q&A sessions and live strategy breakdowns for real-time insights — something most pre-recorded courses simply can’t offer.

Private Discord Community

Lab 2.0 members get access to Upswing’s private Discord server, where you can ask questions, discuss strategies, and connect with fellow grinders working through the same content.The community also features a member blog section where you can track and share your progress — think of it as a modern version of the classic poker forums, but with actual coaches reading and responding.

Pricing

Lab 2.0 is offered as a monthly membership. The membership is priced at $99/month, though you can save significantly by committing to a six-month plan at $399 or a full-year membership at $699. For those on the fence, there is no free trial — but Upswing does back the course with a 30-day satisfaction guarantee for first-time members.

Who Is Lab 2.0 Best For?

Lab 2.0 is an excellent fit for:

  • Beginners who want a structured, no-confusion path to becoming a solid poker player
  • Intermediate grinders stuck at micro or small stakes who need to identify and fix their leaks
  • Live poker players tired of bleeding money against better-prepared opponents
  • Online regs looking to add exploitative depth on top of a sound GTO baseline

It’s worth noting that for medium and high-stakes players, some of the foundational content may feel thin, though the Max Exploit modules and advanced preflop training ensure there’s still genuine value for more experienced players.

What Members Are Saying

The feedback from the Lab 2.0 community has been overwhelmingly positive. One member described it as the best poker course they had seen, adding that access to Uri directly in the private Discord — including personalized answers to game-specific questions — alone justified the investment.

Another member noted that the advanced preflop module inside Lab 2.0 was superior in quality and value to a $499 preflop product they had purchased elsewhere.

The Verdict

Upswing Lab 2.0 is one of the most complete, well-organized poker training memberships available in 2026. The combination of an adaptive learning path, elite coaching from Uri Peleg, interactive tools, live Q&As, and an engaged Discord community makes it stand out in a crowded field. The pricing is fair for the volume and quality of content on offer, especially if you commit to a longer membership.

If you’re looking for a single resource to meaningfully move the needle on your No-Limit Hold’em results, Lab 2.0 is the strongest recommendation we can make.

Overall Rating: 9/10

Ready to take your game to the next level? Check out Upswing Lab 2.0 at upswingpoker

This review is written for informational purposes. Always play responsibly and within your bankroll.

content_html:
If you’re serious about improving your tournament poker game, you’ve probably already heard the name GTO LAB. But does it actually deliver on its promises? We spent time digging into everything the platform offers — coaching content, tools, and value — so you don’t have to guess.

What Is GTO LAB?

GTO LAB (gtolab.com) is a premium online poker training platform built exclusively for tournament (MTT) players. Unlike generalist poker sites that try to cover every format under the sun, GTO LAB has a laser focus: making you a better tournament player by combining elite coaching videos with advanced solver-based training tools.

The platform launched in late 2023 and has quickly become one of the most talked-about names in serious poker study circles — and for good reason.

The Coaching Roster: A Genuine Selling Point

Let’s be blunt — the coaching lineup at GTO LAB is exceptional. We’re not talking about semi-known streamers or mid-stakes regulars. The platform features instruction from some of the biggest names in tournament poker, including Nick Petrangelo, Daniel Dvoress, Jonathan Jaffe, Isaac Haxton, Ben Heath, Leonard Maue, Leon Sturm, Dylan Linde, and Thomas Boivin.

That’s a roster that would make any serious MTT grinder sit up and take notice. These aren’t players dabbling in coaching on the side — they’re actively competing and winning at the highest levels of the game. The coaching library currently spans well over 130 hours of content and continues to grow, covering topics from early-stage hand selection all the way through final table ICM decisions.

Key Features: What You Actually Get

ICM Trainer One of GTO LAB’s standout tools is its full-table ICM trainer — widely considered the most advanced available on any poker training platform. If ICM has always felt like a weak spot in your game (and honestly, it’s a weak spot for most players), this tool alone could justify the subscription cost. You can study how risk premiums shift at different tournament stages, how stack sizes interact with payout pressure, and where most players make costly, avoidable errors.

Postflop cEV Tools In late 2025, GTO LAB launched a fully converged Postflop cEV library after discovering that many popular industry solvers were producing non-converged, unreliable simulations. This is a big deal. If you’ve been studying flop strategy using data from other providers, there’s a real chance some of that information was noise rather than signal. GTO LAB’s postflop tools are built on high-fidelity, accurate data — giving you a cleaner foundation for understanding board textures, range advantages, and bet sizing decisions.

Masterclasses: Tournament Savagery & Multiway Mastery For players who want structured, deep-dive learning rather than a video library to browse, GTO LAB offers standalone masterclasses. Tournament Savagery is a 25-hour course co-created by Daniel Dvoress and another top pro, covering ICM from early stages through final table play in exhaustive detail. Multiway Mastery, taught by Isaac Haxton, tackles one of the most complex and underrated areas of tournament poker: navigating multiway pots with solver-informed thinking. Both are available as standalone purchases for players who don’t want a full subscription.

Who Is GTO LAB Best Suited For?

GTO LAB is built for MTT players who are already past the fundamentals and want to take their game to the next level. If you’re a beginner trying to understand pot odds and basic hand rankings, this probably isn’t where you should start. But if you’re a mid-to-high stakes tournament regular who wants access to elite-level thinking on ICM, bubble play, final table dynamics, and postflop strategy — this platform is hard to beat.

The content covers both online and live tournament formats, applicable across all stake levels, which makes it genuinely versatile for players who move between environments.

GTO LAB vs. Competitors

The most obvious comparison is GTO Wizard, which dominates the broader GTO training market. The key differences worth knowing: GTO LAB offers a full-table ICM trainer that GTO Wizard doesn’t provide, and its coaching content comes exclusively from elite-level tournament professionals rather than a mixed roster of coaches with varying credentials. GTO Wizard has a broader scope for cash game players and beginners; GTO LAB wins decisively on MTT depth and coaching pedigree.

Pricing and Access

GTO LAB offers subscription-based access (Regular and Pro tiers) as well as standalone masterclass purchases. Pro subscribers get full access to the video library. Payment options include standard cards, Luxon, and crypto. The platform also supports subtitles in 10 languages including English, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Italian, Russian, Chinese, Korean, Japanese, and Vietnamese — a nice touch for the global poker community.

The Verdict

GTO LAB has built something genuinely impressive in a relatively short time. The combination of world-class coaching talent, a best-in-class ICM trainer, and now a verified postflop solver library makes it the most complete MTT-focused study platform currently available. It’s not cheap, and it’s not for beginners — but if tournament poker is your primary format and you’re committed to improving, the investment is easy to justify.

Rating: 9/10

Best for: Serious MTT players, mid-to-high stakes tournament grinders, ICM study, final table preparation Not ideal for: Complete beginners, cash game specialists

title: Mastering Double Board Bomb Pots Review: Is PLO Mastermind’s Course Worth It?
excerpt: Double board bomb pots have exploded in popularity at both live and online poker tables over the past few years. These high-variance, action-packed hands create massive pots…
content_html:
Double board bomb pots have exploded in popularity at both live and online poker tables over the past few years. These high-variance, action-packed hands create massive pots and require a completely different strategic approach than standard poker. If you’ve found yourself confused, overwhelmed, or simply punting off chips in these scenarios, PLO Mastermind’s “Mastering Double Board Bomb Pots” course might be exactly what your game needs.

What Are Double Board Bomb Pots?

Before diving into the course review, let’s quickly cover the basics. In a double board bomb pot, all players put in a predetermined amount (usually 2-5 big blinds) before seeing their cards. No preflop action occurs, and then two separate boards are dealt. Players can win both boards, split the pot, or lose entirely. The result? Enormous pots with complex decision trees that can make or break your session.

Course Overview: What’s Inside

PLO Mastermind‘s “Mastering Double Board Bomb Pots” is designed specifically for players who want to gain an edge in these unique situations. The course breaks down the mathematical and strategic complexities of double board scenarios across multiple formats, including PLO, PLO5, and even Hold’em variants.

Key Topics Covered

The training material includes comprehensive modules on:

  • Fundamental Strategy Adjustments: Understanding how double board dynamics change hand values, equity distribution, and optimal play compared to single-board poker
  • Hand Selection and Range Construction: Learning which starting hands gain and lose value in double board scenarios
  • Board Texture Analysis: Identifying favorable and unfavorable runouts across two boards simultaneously
  • Pot Geometry and Bet Sizing: Calculating optimal bet sizes when your equity is split across two boards
  • Positional Considerations: How position becomes even more critical when navigating two boards
  • Variance Management: Understanding the swings inherent to double board play and proper bankroll considerations

What Makes This Course Stand Out

Solver-Backed Analysis

One of the strongest aspects of this training is the heavy reliance on GTO solver work. PLO Mastermind doesn’t just offer opinions or “feel” plays—the course presents solver-derived strategies for common double board situations. This data-driven approach gives you confidence that you’re learning theoretically sound poker rather than outdated conventional wisdom.

Real-World Application

While solver work forms the foundation, the course excels at translating complex theory into practical application. Video breakdowns of actual hands help bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge and real-time decision-making at the tables.

Format Variety

Whether you’re playing double board bomb pots in PLO4, PLO5, or mixed games, the course provides format-specific strategy. This versatility makes it valuable regardless of your primary game.

Who Should Take This Course?

This training is ideal for:

  • Intermediate to advanced PLO players who regularly encounter bomb pots in their games
  • Live cash game players where bomb pots are becoming table standard
  • Players struggling with variance in double board scenarios who want to understand if they’re making mistakes or just running bad
  • Serious students of the game who want to stay ahead of the curve as bomb pots become more prevalent

Who Might Want to Skip It

Conversely, this course may not be the best fit if you:

  • Are a complete beginner to PLO (master single-board fundamentals first)
  • Play exclusively in games where bomb pots don’t run
  • Prefer exploitative strategies over GTO frameworks

Pros and Cons

Advantages

  • Comprehensive coverage of an underserved niche in poker education
  • Solver-based strategies you can trust
  • Practical hand examples that reinforce theoretical concepts
  • Addresses multiple poker formats
  • Helps reduce costly mistakes in high-variance situations

Potential Drawbacks

  • May be too advanced for poker beginners
  • Highly specialized content (won’t improve your overall game if you don’t play bomb pots)
  • Requires solid understanding of PLO fundamentals to extract full value

Value for Money

Double board bomb pots create some of the biggest pots you’ll play all session. A single avoided mistake in one of these hands can easily pay for the entire course. From a pure ROI perspective, if you regularly play in games with bomb pots, the strategic edge you’ll gain should quickly recoup your investment.

The specialized nature of this content also means you’re unlikely to find comparable training elsewhere. PLO Mastermind has essentially created a course for an underserved market segment, which adds to its value proposition.

Final Verdict

“Mastering Double Board Bomb Pots” fills a genuine gap in poker education. As bomb pots continue spreading across poker rooms worldwide, players who understand the unique strategic adjustments required will have a significant advantage over those winging it.

The course combines theoretical rigor with practical application, making it accessible to serious students while remaining grounded in sound poker strategy. If bomb pots are a regular feature in your games and you’re tired of feeling lost in these massive pots, this training offers a clear path to competence and profitability.

Rating: 4.5/5

The course delivers exactly what it promises: a comprehensive, solver-backed approach to mastering one of poker’s most complex and profitable scenarios. The only thing preventing a perfect score is its specialized nature—this is essential training for players who face bomb pots regularly, but unnecessary for those who don’t.

Bottom Line

Double board bomb pots aren’t going anywhere. As these hands become standard in live poker and gain traction online, the edge belongs to prepared players. PLO Mastermind’s “Mastering Double Board Bomb Pots” gives you the tools, frameworks, and confidence to turn these chaotic situations into long-term profit centers.

If you’re serious about improving your bomb pot play and tired of being confused when two boards hit the felt, this course is a worthy investment in your poker education.

Have you taken this course? What’s been your experience with double board bomb pots? Share your thoughts in the comments below.

title: Run It Once Review 2026: Is Phil Galfond’s Training Site Worth It?
excerpt: If you’re serious about improving your poker game, you’ve probably heard of Run It Once. Founded by poker legend Phil Galfond in 2016, this premium training platform has built…
content_html:
If you’re serious about improving your poker game, you’ve probably heard of Run It Once. Founded by poker legend Phil Galfond in 2016, this premium training platform has built a reputation for delivering some of the most advanced poker education available online. But with a competitive training site market and premium pricing, the question remains: is Run It Once worth your investment?

In this comprehensive Run It Once review, we’ll break down everything you need to know about the platform’s content quality, instructor lineup, pricing structure, and whether it’s the right fit for your poker training needs.

What Is Run It Once?

Run It Once (RIO) is a poker training website that offers high-quality instructional videos, strategy articles, and community features designed to help players improve their game across multiple poker variants. The site focuses primarily on No-Limit Hold’em and Pot-Limit Omaha, with content ranging from beginner fundamentals to cutting-edge game theory optimal (GTO) strategies.

What sets Run It Once apart from competitors like PokerCoaching, Upswing Poker, and Red Chip Poker is its emphasis on deep strategic thinking and elite-level instruction. This isn’t a site for casual players looking for quick tips—it’s built for dedicated students of the game willing to put in serious study time.

Content Quality and Course Structure

Video Library

The core of Run It Once’s offering is its extensive video library, featuring thousands of hours of poker instruction. Content is organized into several categories:

Essential courses provide structured learning paths for players at different skill levels. These multi-part series cover everything from preflop ranges to advanced postflop play, with many courses including downloadable materials and practice exercises.

Hand history reviews give you access to real sessions from professional players, complete with detailed thought processes and strategic explanations. Watching elite players work through actual hands provides invaluable insights you simply can’t get from theoretical discussions alone.

Concept videos dive deep into specific strategic topics like ICM considerations, exploitative adjustments, range construction, and mental game fundamentals. These standalone videos allow you to target specific weaknesses in your game.

The production quality across all content is excellent. Videos feature clear audio, easy-to-follow graphics, and professional editing. Instructors use poker software tools to illustrate concepts effectively, making complex strategic ideas accessible even for intermediate players.

Instructor Lineup: Learning from the Best

One of Run It Once’s strongest selling points is its roster of world-class instructors. The site features some of the most respected names in poker:

Phil Galfond, the site’s founder and one of the greatest PLO players in history, regularly contributes content sharing insights from his decades of high-stakes experience. His “Building a Bankroll” series is particularly popular among PLO players.

Sam Greenwood, a tournament crusher with over $40 million in live earnings, offers advanced MTT strategy content that reflects cutting-edge tournament theory.

Ben Sulsky, known as one of the best online cash game players ever, provides No-Limit Hold’em content that emphasizes solid fundamentals and exploitative play.

The instructors don’t just play poker well—they excel at teaching it. Each brings a unique perspective and teaching style, ensuring you’ll find content that resonates with your learning preferences.

Run It Once Pricing: What Does It Cost?

Run It Once operates on a subscription model with three membership tiers:

Essential Membership provides access to the core video library and community features. This entry-level option works well for players just getting started with structured poker training.

Elite Membership unlocks the complete video library, including advanced courses, elite-level content, and all new releases. For serious players, this tier offers the best value given the depth of material available.

Essential Plus sits between the two options, offering more content than Essential but not quite everything Elite provides.

Pricing is competitive with other premium poker training sites, though Run It Once tends to position itself at the higher end of the market. The site occasionally runs promotional offers, so it’s worth checking for discounts before subscribing.

One advantage: there’s no long-term commitment required. You can subscribe month-to-month and cancel anytime, allowing you to access content during intensive study periods without paying year-round.

Platform Features and User Experience

Beyond video content, Run It Once offers several features that enhance the learning experience:

The hand replayer tool allows you to upload your own hands and work through them using RIO’s interface, making it easier to analyze your play alongside the concepts you’re learning.

The community forums provide a space to discuss strategy with other serious players. While not as active as some competitor communities, the quality of discussion tends to be high given the site’s focus on dedicated students.

Mobile access is available, allowing you to watch videos on tablets or smartphones. The mobile experience works reasonably well, though some of the software demonstrations are easier to follow on a full-sized screen.

The site’s search and filtering capabilities make it relatively easy to find content on specific topics, though the sheer volume of material can feel overwhelming for new members.

Run It Once vs. Competitors

How does Run It Once stack up against alternatives?

Compared to PokerCoaching (formerly Upswing Lab): RIO offers more advanced content and a stronger instructor lineup for cash games, while PokerCoaching provides more structured learning paths and better beginner-to-intermediate content.

Compared to Red Chip Poker: Run It Once is more expensive but delivers significantly more advanced material. Red Chip excels at fundamentals and mid-stakes strategy, while RIO better serves players looking to compete at higher levels.

Compared to MasterClass format sites: Unlike one-off purchases, RIO requires ongoing subscription, but you get access to constantly updated content and a much deeper library of material.

The right choice depends on your current skill level and goals. Beginning players may find better value elsewhere, while serious students aiming for mid-to-high stakes will appreciate Run It Once’s depth.

Who Should Subscribe to Run It Once?

Run It Once is ideal for:

  • Cash game players (especially NLHE and PLO specialists) looking to move up in stakes
  • Tournament players willing to invest serious study time into advanced concepts
  • Players already comfortable with poker fundamentals who want to refine their strategy
  • Anyone interested in learning GTO principles and solver-based approaches
  • Dedicated students willing to put in work beyond just watching videos

Run It Once may not be the best fit for:

  • Complete beginners who need foundational poker education
  • Recreational players seeking quick tips rather than comprehensive strategy
  • Players on tight budgets looking for free or low-cost alternatives
  • Those who learn better through interactive coaching rather than video content

The Verdict: Is Run It Once Worth It?

For the right player, Run It Once delivers exceptional value. The combination of elite instructors, comprehensive content coverage, and focus on advanced strategy makes it one of the best poker training platforms available.

The site’s main weaknesses are its premium pricing and the overwhelming amount of content that can make it difficult to create a structured study plan without discipline. The platform also lacks some of the interactive elements and community engagement found on competing sites.

That said, if you’re a serious player committed to improving your game and willing to invest both money and study time, Run It Once provides the tools and knowledge you need to compete at higher levels. The quality of instruction and depth of strategic coverage justify the cost for players who will actively use the platform.

Rating: 4.5/5 stars

The bottom line? Run It Once isn’t for everyone, but for dedicated poker students aiming to elevate their game, it’s one of the best investments you can make in your poker education. Start with a monthly subscription to explore the platform, and upgrade to Elite if you find the content valuable for your specific games and stakes.

Ready to take your poker game to the next level? Visit Run It Once to explore their current membership options and see if this premium training platform is right for you.

Have you tried Run It Once or other poker training sites? Share your experiences in the comments below!

title: You’re Thinking About Preflop the Wrong Way
excerpt: If you’re still memorizing preflop charts like they’re the Ten Commandments of poker, you’re leaving money on the table. The truth is, most players approach preflop strategy…
content_html:
If you’re still memorizing preflop charts like they’re the Ten Commandments of poker, you’re leaving money on the table. The truth is, most players approach preflop strategy completely backward—treating it as a rigid system of rules rather than what it actually is: a dynamic chess match that changes with every opponent.

The Chart Memorization Trap

Walk into any poker room, and you’ll find players glued to their phones between hands, studying color-coded charts that tell them exactly which hands to play from which positions. While these charts provide a solid baseline, they’re designed for one specific scenario—playing against theoretically optimal opponents who don’t exist at your table.

The real edge in poker comes from adaptability, not memorization. Let’s explore how the best players actually think about preflop.

Think Like a Chess Player: Identify the Threats

In chess, every move is evaluated based on the threats it creates or defends against. Poker works the same way. Before you decide on your preflop action, ask yourself: “What threats does this opponent pose?”

When the Threat Exists

You can’t profitably open-raise 3x or 4x with a wide range in theory because competent players will punish you with 3-bets. This threat forces you to tighten up or face difficult decisions with marginal holdings.

When the Threat Disappears

But what happens when you’re facing a calling station who never 3-bets? Suddenly, that threat evaporates. This is your green light to exploit them by increasing your opening size to 2.5x or even 3x, extracting maximum value from their overly loose calling range.

The key insight: your strategy should shift based on whether specific threats are present or absent.

The Betting Volume Principle: Follow the Money

Here’s a simple but powerful framework that will transform your preflop decision-making: place your strongest hands wherever your opponent puts the most money into the pot, and play your weakest hands in whatever way lets you see the flop cheapest.

Premium Hands Want Action

Your aces and kings don’t care about how they get paid—they just want to get paid. This means:

Against aggressive opponents who attack limpers: Limp your monsters. If an opponent frequently raises over limps but plays passively against standard opens, trap them by limping your premium hands and letting them do the raising for you.

Against passive opponents who rarely raise limpers: Open-raise your strong hands. If they’re not going to build the pot for you, you need to build it yourself.

Weak Hands Want Cheap Equity

The bottom of your range has different goals. These marginal holdings want to realize their equity as cheaply as possible. If an opponent allows you to see flops for just the small blind without raising, you can limp a very wide range and play profitable poker postflop.

Facing Maniacs: The Counterintuitive Adjustment

When you encounter a hyperaggressive player who 3-bets or raises at an absurd frequency, your instinct might be to tighten up and wait for premiums. That’s half right.

The full adjustment is this: open tighter and fold less.

Here’s why: every time you open a hand and then fold to a 3-bet, you’re rewarding the maniac’s aggression with free money. You’re essentially donating chips to reinforce their profitable strategy.

Instead, restrict your opening range to hands strong enough to defend against a raise—either by calling or 4-betting. If an opponent’s 3-bet percentage exceeds your opening percentage, your fold-to-3-bet frequency should theoretically drop to zero. You’re only playing hands you’re willing to continue with.

Range Construction: Blockers vs. Playability

The types of hands you should play change dramatically based on your opponent’s tendencies.

Against Aggressive Players: Prioritize Blockers

When facing heavy 3-betting, solvers reveal a preference for hands with high-card blockers—think Ace-x and King-x combinations. These hands reduce the likelihood your opponent holds a premium hand, making their aggression less credible and your defends more profitable.

Blockers become your shield against relentless pressure.

Against Passive Players: Prioritize Playability

If your opponents are calling stations who let you see flops cheaply, blockers matter far less. Here, you should shift toward hands with excellent playability and implied odds.

Suited connectors like 65s suddenly become more valuable than offsuit Broadway cards because they perform better in multiway pots and create disguised strong hands when they connect with the board.

Exploit with Sizing: One Size Doesn’t Fit All

Perhaps the most underutilized adjustment in preflop strategy is varying your raise size based on opponent tendencies.

Against Fish and Calling Stations

If the player in the big blind consistently overpays for their equity and rarely raises, punish them by overcharging. Increase your opening size to extract maximum value from their willingness to call too wide with inferior hands.

Against Nits and Tight Players

Conversely, if opponents are folding too frequently, you can open an extremely wide range—up to 71% or more—and potentially use smaller sizes to steal blinds efficiently and cheaply.

The Real Secret: Brain Solving Over Chart Following

The common thread running through all these adjustments is that effective preflop strategy requires real-time problem-solving, not robotic chart following.

Every table is different. Every opponent presents unique opportunities for exploitation. The player who wins isn’t the one with the most charts memorized—it’s the one who can rapidly identify opponent tendencies and adjust accordingly.

Start viewing preflop as a dynamic environment where your strategy is in constant flux. Ask yourself before every decision:

  • What threats does this opponent pose?
  • Where will this opponent put the most money in the pot?
  • Am I opening hands I’m prepared to defend?
  • Does this opponent’s style call for blockers or playability?
  • Can I exploit them with sizing adjustments?

Conclusion: From Static to Dynamic

The difference between break-even players and consistent winners often comes down to preflop adjustments. While everyone else is consulting their charts and playing robotic poker, you can be identifying exploits and printing money.

Stop thinking about preflop as a memorization exercise. Start thinking about it as a chess match where you identify threats, follow the money, and constantly adjust to the unique conditions at your table.

That’s when your win rate will truly take off.

Ready to take your poker game to the next level? Understanding dynamic preflop strategy is just the beginning. Master these concepts, and you’ll never look at preflop the same way again.

title: Advanced Tournament Course Review: Is PokerCoaching.com’s Premium Training Worth It?
excerpt: Tournament poker has evolved dramatically over the past decade, and staying competitive requires more than just understanding basic strategy. PokerCoaching.com’s Advanced…
content_html:
Tournament poker has evolved dramatically over the past decade, and staying competitive requires more than just understanding basic strategy. PokerCoaching.com’s Advanced Tournament Course promises to elevate your game with cutting-edge concepts taught by some of the best minds in poker. But does it deliver on that promise?

What You Get

The Advanced Tournament Course is designed for players who’ve moved beyond the fundamentals and are ready to tackle the nuanced situations that separate good tournament players from great ones. The curriculum dives deep into ICM considerations, exploitative adjustments, range construction in high-pressure spots, and the psychological aspects of tournament play that often get overlooked in beginner materials.

What sets this course apart is its focus on real-world application. Rather than drowning students in theoretical GTO charts, the instructors break down actual hands from major tournaments, showing you how elite players think through complex decisions in real time. This approach bridges the gap between knowing what to do and actually executing at the table.

The Teaching Approach

The course material is structured progressively, allowing you to build on concepts systematically. Each module includes video lessons, quizzes to test your understanding, and hand history reviews that challenge you to apply what you’ve learned. The production quality is professional, and the instructors communicate complex ideas in accessible language without dumbing down the content.

One standout feature is the emphasis on adjusting your strategy based on stack depths, bubble factors, and opponent tendencies. Too many players learn a one-size-fits-all approach, but this course teaches you to think dynamically and make exploitative plays when the situation calls for it.

Who Should Take This Course

This isn’t a course for complete beginners. If you’re still learning position, hand rankings, or basic bet sizing, you’ll want to master those fundamentals first. The Advanced Tournament Course is ideal for intermediate players who consistently cash in smaller tournaments but struggle to make deep runs or final tables, as well as experienced players looking to refine specific aspects of their game.

Players who primarily focus on cash games might find some concepts less applicable, though the theoretical foundations translate across formats.

The Bottom Line

PokerCoaching.com’s Advanced Tournament Course represents a significant investment in your poker education, but for serious tournament players, the ROI potential is substantial. The quality of instruction, depth of content, and practical approach make this one of the more comprehensive tournament training resources available today.

If you’re committed to taking your tournament game to the next level and you’re willing to put in the study time, this course provides the roadmap. Just remember that consuming content isn’t enough—you’ll need to put these concepts into practice and continue refining your approach at the tables.

For players serious about tournament poker, this course earns a strong recommendation. It won’t magically transform you into a champion overnight, but it will give you the tools and framework to compete at a higher level.

title: Elliot Roe’s A-Game Poker Masterclass Review: Can Mental Game Training Transform Your Poker Results?
excerpt: Rating: 4.5/5 When it comes to poker training, most players obsess over GTO strategies, range charts, and solver outputs. But what happens when you know the right play but…
content_html:
Rating: 4.5/5

When it comes to poker training, most players obsess over GTO strategies, range charts, and solver outputs. But what happens when you know the right play but can’t execute it under pressure? That’s where Elliot Roe’s A-Game Poker Masterclass from Run It Once comes in—a course that tackles the mental side of poker that often separates winning players from those stuck in mediocrity.

What Is the A-Game Poker Masterclass?

The A-Game Poker Masterclass is a comprehensive mental performance program designed specifically for poker players. Created by renowned performance coach Elliot Roe in partnership with Run It Once, this course goes beyond traditional poker strategy to address the psychological barriers that prevent players from performing at their peak.

Unlike standard poker courses that focus solely on technical play, this masterclass combines sports psychology, mindfulness techniques, and practical mental game strategies to help players overcome tilt, maintain focus during long sessions, and develop the mental resilience needed for consistent results.

Who Is Elliot Roe?

Elliot Roe is a performance coach who has worked with some of the biggest names in poker, including Fedor Holz, Chance Kornuth, and Jeff Gross. With over a decade of experience helping players optimize their mental game, Roe has become the go-to expert for elite players looking to gain a competitive edge through mental training.

His approach combines hypnotherapy, visualization, and cognitive behavioral techniques to help players break through mental barriers and achieve peak performance states consistently.

Course Structure and Content

The A-Game Poker Masterclass is divided into multiple modules that progressively build your mental game foundation:

Core Modules Include:

  • Understanding the mental game and why it matters for poker success
  • Identifying your personal mental game leaks and triggers
  • Building pre-session routines that prime you for optimal performance
  • Managing tilt and emotional control during downswings
  • Developing focus and concentration for long grinding sessions
  • Creating effective meditation and mindfulness practices
  • Visualization techniques for confidence building
  • Post-session analysis and mental game review processes

Each module combines video lessons, practical exercises, and guided meditation sessions that you can use during your poker sessions.

What Makes This Course Different?

1. Poker-Specific Mental Training

While generic sports psychology can be helpful, Roe’s program is tailored specifically for the unique challenges poker players face—variance, long-term thinking, game selection anxiety, and the isolation of online grinding.

2. Actionable Tools, Not Just Theory

The course doesn’t just explain concepts; it provides downloadable audio sessions, worksheets, and routines you can implement immediately. The guided meditation tracks are particularly valuable for pre-session preparation.

3. Addresses Real Player Problems

Whether you struggle with shot-taking anxiety, results-oriented thinking, or maintaining discipline during downswings, the course tackles the mental game issues that actually affect your bottom line.

Pros and Cons

Pros:

  • Comprehensive coverage of mental game fundamentals
  • Practical exercises and guided audio sessions
  • Proven techniques used by elite players
  • Addresses poker-specific mental challenges
  • Lifetime access with Run It Once membership
  • Complements technical poker training perfectly

Cons:

  • Requires consistent practice to see results
  • Some techniques may feel uncomfortable initially for skeptical players
  • Best results come from long-term implementation, not quick fixes
  • Premium pricing may be prohibitive for micro-stakes players

Who Should Take This Course?

This masterclass is ideal for:

  • Players who know the right plays but struggle to execute them consistently
  • Grinders experiencing burnout or motivation issues
  • Anyone who has lost significant money due to tilt
  • Players preparing to move up in stakes
  • Those who want to maximize their technical knowledge with mental game optimization

It’s less suitable for complete beginners who haven’t yet developed a solid technical foundation, as mental game training works best when you already understand correct poker strategy.

Is It Worth the Investment?

Here’s the reality: if poor mental game has cost you even a few buy-ins, this course pays for itself quickly. The difference between playing your A-game versus your C-game can easily be worth several big blinds per 100 hands—that’s thousands of dollars over time for serious players.

The course requires commitment and practice, but for players serious about improving their consistency and results, the A-Game Poker Masterclass addresses the often-overlooked 50% of poker success that happens between your ears.

Final Verdict

Elliot Roe’s A-Game Poker Masterclass is one of the most comprehensive mental game resources available for poker players. While it won’t teach you how to 3-bet bluff the button or balance your river range, it will help you actually execute those plays when it matters most.

For players who have invested heavily in technical training but still struggle with consistency, tilt, or mental resilience, this course fills a crucial gap in their poker education. title: How to CRUSH Limpers in Small Stakes Cash Games
excerpt: Open-limping is one of the most common mistakes you’ll encounter at small stakes cash games. While it might be tempting to “loosen up” and play more hands against these weak…
content_html:
Open-limping is one of the most common mistakes you’ll encounter at small stakes cash games. While it might be tempting to “loosen up” and play more hands against these weak players, the path to crushing limpers lies in disciplined, fundamentally sound poker that systematically exploits their specific weaknesses.

In this comprehensive guide, you’ll learn exactly how to punish limpers, build massive pots with your value hands, and navigate tricky post-flop situations to maximize your win rate.

Why Limpers Are Exploitable (And How to Take Advantage)

Understanding why limping is a mistake is crucial to exploiting it effectively. When a player open-limps, they’re signaling they have a marginal hand—not garbage they’d fold, and not a premium they’d raise. This capped range creates immediate opportunities for you to profit.

Your strategy shouldn’t be to “get loose” or “fight fire with fire.” Instead, you need to punish limpers by isolating them with strong hands and forcing them to play large pots out of position with inferior holdings.

Pre-Flop Strategy: The Isolation Play

Raise Sizing That Commands Respect

The foundation of crushing limpers starts with proper raise sizing. You need to raise large enough to discourage multi-way pots while building value with your superior hands.

In Position: Raise to 4.5x the big blind plus 1 big blind for every additional limper.

Out of Position: Raise to roughly 5x the big blind plus 1 big blind per limper.

For example, in a $1/$2 game with five limpers ahead of you, raise to approximately $16-$18 to properly isolate. This sizing achieves two critical goals: it charges limpers the maximum for their marginal hands, and it ensures you’re playing heads-up or in favorable 3-way scenarios rather than dangerous multi-way pots.

Constructing Your Isolation Range

Your raising range against limpers should be linear—meaning you’re raising your strongest hands in order of equity. Forget polarized ranges here; limpers call too often with medium-strength hands to make bluffs profitable.

Raise with: Pocket 6s and better, A7s+, A5s, AJo+, K9s+, KQo, and suited broadway hands.

Over-limp with: Small pairs, suited connectors, and some suited Aces or Kings that play well multi-way but lack the raw equity to raise for value.

Resist the urge to get “fancy” by raising garbage hands. Limpers are calling stations by nature—they’ll call with anything remotely playable, making your weak raises simply light money on fire.

Position-Based Adjustments for Trapping

Not all limps are created equal. A player limping from late position (cutoff or button) is rarely trapping with premium hands. They’re afraid of the blinds coming along cheaply and cracking their big pair in a multi-way pot. Attack these limpers aggressively.

Early position limpers deserve more caution. While most recreational players aren’t sophisticated enough to trap consistently, the occasional limp-call with Aces or Kings does happen from early position. Don’t let this fear paralyze you, but exercise slightly more discretion.

Post-Flop Domination: Leveraging Your Range Advantage

Once you successfully isolate a limper, you enter the post-flop phase with a massive range advantage. You raised the top 24% of hands while they limped marginal holdings. This disparity allows you to apply consistent pressure.

Continuation Betting Like a Pro

Your c-betting strategy should adapt to board texture and how it connects with your range versus theirs.

High-Card Dynamic Boards (A-J-7, K-Q-4): These boards smash your isolation range. You have all the Aces, Kings, and premium pairs while the limper’s range is capped. Bet aggressively on these textures, using both large and small sizing depending on your specific holding.

Low-Card Boards (7-7-6, 5-4-2, 8-6-3): Pump the brakes here. Your raising range contains very few low cards, while the limper’s range is full of small pairs and suited connectors. Check these boards more frequently and proceed with caution when facing resistance.

The Flush Board Dilemma

Monotone (three-flush) boards require extreme caution against limpers. Recreational players love suited cards—it’s one of the main reasons they’re limping in the first place.

When you see three clubs, three hearts, or any three-suited board, check a high percentage of your range. If you do bet, bet small. Your opponent often has flushes or strong draws in these scenarios, eliminating your typical nut advantage.

Reading Limper Behavior: Specific Situations

The Donk Bet

When a limper leads into you on the flop (donk betting), pay attention. GTO solvers donk bet roughly 0.3% of the time—meaning it’s almost never theoretically correct. In practice at small stakes, a donk bet usually signals a specific hand strength, often a strong made hand or draw.

Don’t automatically assume weakness. Proceed with caution or raise if you can clearly define their range as weak, but treat this unusual line with respect.

River Aggression from Passive Players

If a limper checks and calls the flop and turn, then suddenly leads out or raises on the river, they’re rarely bluffing. In small stakes games, when passive players show aggression on the river, they almost always have a strong hand.

Fold your marginal made hands. Save your chips for better spots.

The Rake Factor: Why Raising Beats Limping

Here’s a crucial mathematical reality often overlooked: the rake structure in small stakes games heavily favors playing fewer, larger pots over many small pots.

Casinos typically take 10% of every pot, often capped at $5-$6. When you limp along and play small pots, the rake consumes a devastating percentage of your potential profit. By raising and playing larger pots, you minimize the rake’s impact on your win rate.

Think of it this way: would you rather win ten $10 pots (losing $10 to rake) or two $50 pots (losing $10-$12 to rake)? The math is clear—raise to build big pots with your strong hands.

The Psychology of Exploitation

Imagine a limper as someone trying to sneak into a movie theater through the side door. They haven’t paid the full price of admission (a raise), so they likely don’t have a premium ticket (a strong hand). Your job as the crusher is to act as security: force them to pay a high price to see the screen (the flop).

When they do pay, you know they’re overpaying for a mediocre view while you’re sitting in the VIP section with a premium pass. This mental framework keeps you aggressive and value-focused.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Playing too loose yourself. Don’t fall into the trap of thinking you need to loosen up to “match” the table’s loosey-goosey style. Maintain discipline.

Raising too small. Undersized raises allow multiple limpers to call profitably, creating exactly the multi-way pot you’re trying to avoid.

Over-c-betting on bad boards. Not every flop deserves a continuation bet. Check low-card and three-flush boards more often.

Paying off river aggression. When the calling station suddenly bets or raises the river, believe them.

Putting It All Together

Crushing limpers in small stakes cash games isn’t about fancy plays or creative strategies—it’s about fundamentally sound poker executed with discipline. Isolate with proper sizing, construct linear value ranges, apply appropriate post-flop pressure based on board texture, and respect unusual aggression from passive opponents.

The beauty of this strategy is its consistency. Limpers aren’t going anywhere in small stakes games, which means you have an endless supply of profitable situations waiting for you. Master these concepts, apply them with discipline, and watch your win rate soar.

Remember: every time you see that familiar limp, you’re not seeing a problem—you’re seeing an opportunity to print money.

Now get out there and crush those limpers!

Frequently Asked Questions

Should I ever limp behind other limpers?

Yes, but selectively. Over-limping with small pairs, suited connectors, and some suited Aces or Kings makes sense because these hands play well multi-way but lack the raw equity to raise for value. However, this should be the exception, not your default strategy.

What if multiple players limp? Should I still raise?

Absolutely. In fact, you should raise even larger—add one big blind to your raise size for each additional limper. With five limpers, you might be raising to $16-$18 in a $1/$2 game. This sizing is necessary to avoid creating a profitable multi-way pot.

How often should I c-bet after isolating a limper?

Your c-betting frequency should depend heavily on board texture. On high-card dynamic boards, bet very frequently. On low-card boards and three-flush boards, check much more often. There’s no fixed percentage—adjust based on how the board connects with your range versus the limper’s range.

What if the limper is actually trapping with a premium hand?

This happens rarely enough that it shouldn’t change your overall strategy. Late position limpers are almost never trapping (they fear multi-way pots). Early position limpers trap slightly more often, but it’s still uncommon at small stakes. Play fundamentally sound poker and accept that you’ll occasionally run into a trap—the long-term profits far outweigh these occasional setbacks.

Is it worth isolating limpers if the rake is high?

Absolutely—in fact, high rake makes isolation even more important. By raising and playing larger pots, you minimize the rake’s percentage impact on your wins. Limping along and playing many small pots means the rake eats up a much larger portion of your profit.

title: Precision Poker Review 2026: Is Upswing’s Mastering Methodology Course Worth It?
