Looking for an honest Precision Poker review? In this comprehensive guide, we’ll break down everything you need to know about Upswing Poker’s innovative training course by Alexandre Vuilleumier, including pricing, content, and who should (and shouldn’t) invest in this poker methodology program.

What Is Precision Poker?

Precision Poker – Mastering Methodology is a revolutionary poker training course created by Alexandre Vuilleumier for Upswing Poker. Unlike traditional poker courses that teach you what to do, this program teaches you how to think and develop your own winning strategies.

Who Is Alexandre Vuilleumier?

Alexandre Vuilleumier brings a unique perspective to poker training:

  • International Chess Master with a peak rating of 2,400
  • WSOP bracelet winner (2023 $25K High Roller)
  • Over $2.3 million in live tournament earnings
  • Former chess coach with 10 years of teaching experience
  • Started playing high-stakes poker seriously in 2021

Precision Poker Course Content: What You’ll Learn

The Precision Poker course includes 18 comprehensive modules designed around active learning and practical exercises. Here’s what the curriculum covers:

Core Training Modules

  1. Creative Destruction – Breaking down bad habits and outdated poker concepts
  2. Pen & Paper Exercise – Documenting your decision-making process
  3. PioSolver Exercises – Learning to counter unconventional strategies
  4. Aggregated Reports Analysis – Working with macro-level data
  5. GTO vs Exploitative Play – Understanding when to apply each approach
  6. Mass Database Analysis (MDA) – Identifying patterns in large datasets
  7. Turn Barrel Exercise – Advanced postflop play
  8. Opponent Ranging – Which datapoints matter most
  9. Opponent Preparation – Pre-session game planning
  10. The Ultimate Trifecta – Combining GTO, MDA, and Opponent-Specific Reads
  11. Pattern Library Building – Bottom-up approach to strategy development
  12. Blocker Study – Top-down theoretical framework
  13. Preflop Theory – Foundational range construction
  14. Preflop Trifecta – Applied preflop methodology
  15. Multiway Pots – The sandwich dilemma and complex situations
  16. ICM Study – Tournament-specific concepts
  17. Tournament Session Review – Real-world application
  18. Cash Game Session Review – Hands-on analysis

Software and Tools Integration

Unlike courses that rely on solvers alone, Precision Poker teaches you to master multiple poker tools:

  • Flopzilla / PowerEquilab – Hand-building strategies for deeper understanding
  • PioSolver – GTO analysis and solver-based exercises
  • Hold’em Resources Calculator – ICM calculations
  • Hand2Note – Database tracking and analysis
  • Excel – Custom analysis and pattern recognition

The Precision Poker Philosophy: Why It’s Different

What sets Precision Poker apart from other poker training courses is its fundamental philosophy. Drawing from his chess background, Alexandre Vuilleumier emphasizes:

Active Learning Over Passive Consumption

Instead of watching videos and copying strategies, you’ll complete hands-on exercises that force you to think critically and develop your own solutions. This approach helps you:

  • Internalize concepts at a deeper level
  • Build confidence in your decision-making
  • Develop a unique playing style
  • Adapt strategies to your specific games

Creativity and Innovation

Alex believes modern poker players are too focused on copying what works for others rather than innovating. The course encourages you to:

  • Question conventional wisdom
  • Experiment with new approaches
  • Find edges others haven’t discovered
  • Make poker more intellectually rewarding

Precision Poker Pricing and Value

The Precision Poker course costs $499 for lifetime access with no recurring fees or subscriptions. You get:

  • Downloadable exercises and workbooks
  • Pre-built aggregated reports to get started
  • English subtitles and transcripts for all videos
  • Self-paced learning (recommended 2+ hours per week)
  • 30-day satisfaction guarantee for first-time buyers

Bonus: Upswing occasionally offers the “Exploit & Conquer” course (normally $299) as a free bonus with purchase.

Who Should Buy Precision Poker?

Ideal Students

This course is perfect for poker players who:

  • ✅ Want to develop their own unique playing style
  • ✅ Enjoy working with poker software and analysis tools
  • ✅ Learn best through hands-on exercises and practice
  • ✅ Play No Limit Hold’em cash games or tournaments
  • ✅ Are willing to invest time in active learning
  • ✅ Feel frustrated by cookie-cutter poker advice
  • ✅ Play at any stake level (micro to high stakes)
  • ✅ Prefer understanding why over memorizing what

Not Recommended For

Skip this course if you:

  • ❌ Are a complete poker beginner
  • ❌ Want plug-and-play strategies to memorize
  • ❌ Prefer passive video watching without exercises
  • ❌ Don’t want to invest time with software tools
  • ❌ Need immediate results without putting in work
  • ❌ Only play casual home games

Precision Poker vs Other Training Sites

How It Compares to Upswing Poker Lab

While Upswing’s Poker Lab focuses on teaching specific strategies and plays, Precision Poker teaches you the methodology to develop your own strategies. Think of it this way:

  • Poker Lab: “Here’s how to play this situation”
  • Precision Poker: “Here’s how to figure out the best play for any situation”

Unique Advantages

  • Chess master’s analytical approach
  • Emphasis on creative strategy development
  • Focus on learning methodology, not just tactics
  • Applicable to any stake level or game variant
  • Builds long-term analytical skills

Precision Poker Review: Pros and Cons

Pros

  • ✅ Unique methodology-focused approach – Teaches you how to learn, not just what to learn
  • ✅ Instructor credibility – Taught by a WSOP bracelet winner and chess master
  • ✅ Comprehensive tool training – Learn to maximize PioSolver, Flopzilla, databases, and more
  • ✅ Applicable to all stakes – Methodology works from micro stakes to nosebleeds
  • ✅ Lifetime access – No recurring subscription fees
  • ✅ Develops critical thinking – Makes you a better poker thinker, not just a copycat
  • ✅ Both cash and tournament content – Covers all major game formats

Cons

  • ❌ High upfront cost – $499 is steep for recreational players
  • ❌ Requires significant time investment – Not a quick-fix solution
  • ❌ Steep learning curve – Exercises are challenging and require effort
  • ❌ Limited reviews available – Course is relatively new (launched 2024)
  • ❌ Software costs – You’ll need to purchase tools like PioSolver separately
  • ❌ Not beginner-friendly – Assumes basic poker knowledge

Student Results and Testimonials

As a newer course (launched in February 2024), independent student reviews are limited. However, based on Upswing Poker’s track record and Alexandre Vuilleumier’s credentials, the methodology appears sound for serious students willing to put in the work.

The course emphasizes that results depend entirely on your effort completing the exercises and applying the methodology consistently.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Precision Poker worth the $499 price tag?

If you’re serious about poker improvement and willing to invest significant time in active learning, yes. The methodology-focused approach provides long-term value that transcends specific strategies. However, recreational players or those wanting quick tips should look elsewhere.

How long does it take to complete Precision Poker?

At the recommended pace of 2+ hours per week, you can complete the core material in 2-3 months. However, mastering the methodology and completing all exercises thoroughly may take 6+ months of dedicated study.

Do I need PioSolver to take this course?

While some exercises use PioSolver, the course also teaches alternative tools like Flopzilla and PowerEquilab. You don’t need every tool to benefit, but you’ll get more value with access to solver software.

Can beginners take Precision Poker?

No. The course assumes you understand basic poker concepts, hand ranges, and position. Complete beginners should start with Upswing’s Poker Lab or similar foundational courses first.

Does Precision Poker include hand reviews?

Yes, the course includes both tournament and cash game session reviews demonstrating how to apply the methodology to real hands. However, the focus is on teaching you the review process rather than just showing you specific hands.

Final Verdict: Should You Buy Precision Poker?

Precision Poker – Mastering Methodology represents a paradigm shift in poker training. Instead of feeding you strategies to memorize, it teaches you to think like a poker theorist and develop your own winning approach.

Buy Precision Poker if you:

  • Are committed to long-term poker improvement
  • Want to develop a unique, personal playing style
  • Enjoy analytical thinking and problem-solving
  • Have the discipline to complete challenging exercises
  • Play poker seriously (even at lower stakes)

Skip this course if you:

  • Want quick, easy answers
  • Prefer copying proven strategies
  • Are a complete beginner
  • Don’t enjoy working with software tools

Alternative Options

If Precision Poker doesn’t fit your needs, consider:

  • Upswing Poker Lab 2.0 – More structured, strategy-focused training for all levels
  • Run It Once – Comprehensive video library with high-level play
  • PokerCoaching.com – Tournament-focused training with Jonathan Little
  • Red Chip Poker – Budget-friendly option for small stakes players

Where to Buy Precision Poker

The official Precision Poker course is available exclusively through Upswing Poker’s website. Watch for promotional periods when they include the Exploit & Conquer bonus course.

Current Price: $499 (lifetime access)
Money-Back Guarantee: 30 days for first-time buyers

Conclusion

Precision Poker by Alexandre Vuilleumier is one of the most intellectually ambitious poker training courses available. It won’t make you a winner overnight, but it will fundamentally change how you think about poker strategy development.

For serious students ready to invest time and effort into mastering the craft of poker strategy creation, this course offers exceptional long-term value. The methodology you’ll learn applies to any game, any stake level, and any future evolution of poker theory.

However, if you’re looking for paint-by-numbers strategies or quick fixes, your money is better spent elsewhere. Precision Poker rewards dedication, curiosity, and intellectual engagement—qualities that will serve you well both at and away from the poker table.

Rating: 4.5/5 for serious students | 2/5 for casual players

What Is Elite Cash Game Exploits?

Elite Cash Game Exploits is an advanced cash game poker training course created by Uri Peleg for Upswing Poker. Unlike traditional poker courses that focus heavily on Game Theory Optimal (GTO) play, this course teaches players how to profitably deviate from GTO strategies to exploit opponent weaknesses.

About Uri Peleg: Your Poker Coach

Uri Peleg is a high-stakes crusher with the bulk of his play at $25/50, bringing real-world credibility to the table. Peleg rose to the game’s highest ranks in the pre-solver era of poker, using an exploitative approach that adjusted his play to make maximum money from each opponent.

What Makes Elite Cash Game Exploits Different?

Beyond GTO: The Exploitative Approach

While most modern poker training revolves around solvers and GTO solutions, Peleg’s approach marks quite a departure from the game theory optimal strategies that dominate most modern-era poker training materials.

The course doesn’t reject GTO—instead, it builds upon it. Peleg emphasizes that GTO is an important baseline that all players should learn, but once you master these fundamentals, you can start looking for ways to deviate from it to maximize profit against real opponents who make mistakes.

Hard vs. Soft Exploits

One of the core concepts introduced early in the course is the distinction between:

  • Hard exploits – Maximally exploiting opponent mistakes, though more easily detectable
  • Soft exploits – Subtle adjustments that are harder for opponents to notice and counter

This framework runs throughout the entire course and helps you choose the right approach for different game dynamics.

What is the best Cory Mikesell poker book for beginners?

Are Cory Mikesell’s books suitable for cash games or tournaments?

What is solver-based poker strategy?

Solver-based strategy uses computer programs (solvers) to calculate mathematically optimal plays in poker situations. Mikesell’s books translate these complex solutions into practical strategies.

No. While Mikesell uses solvers in his research, his books are designed for players without solver access. The Five Card Formula specifically teaches how to study without solvers.

Yes, for serious PLO players. His pioneering work on solver-based strategy and coverage of understudied variants like 5c and 6c PLO provides significant edge over opponents. Given his $1,000/hour coaching rate, his books offer exceptional value.

title: Road to Victory Review: Is This Upswing Poker Tournament Course Worth It?
excerpt: If you’re serious about crushing poker tournaments in 2025, Darren Elias and Nick Petrangelo’s Road to Victory course from Upswing Poker might be exactly what your game needs.…
content_html:
If you’re serious about crushing poker tournaments in 2025, Darren Elias and Nick Petrangelo’s Road to Victory course from Upswing Poker might be exactly what your game needs. After analyzing this comprehensive tournament training program, I’m breaking down everything you need to know before investing in this elite-level course.

What Is Road to Victory?

Road to Victory is Upswing Poker’s flagship tournament poker training course, designed and taught by two of the game’s most accomplished MTT professionals. Darren Elias holds the all-time record for World Poker Tour titles (four and counting), while Nick Petrangelo has amassed over $20 million in live tournament earnings. Together, they’ve created what many consider the most comprehensive tournament poker course available today.

The course targets intermediate to advanced players looking to take their tournament game to the next level, covering everything from early-stage play through ICM-heavy final table decisions.

What’s Included in the Course?

Road to Victory delivers over 50 hours of premium poker training content, structured into detailed modules that cover every phase of tournament play:

Core Curriculum:

  • Preflop ranges and adjustments for all tournament stages
  • Early and middle stage strategy optimization
  • Bubble play and ICM fundamentals
  • Final table dynamics and deal-making
  • Live poker tells and physical reads
  • Mental game and variance management
  • Hand history reviews from major tournaments

The course includes both theoretical lessons and practical hand breakdowns from real high-stakes tournaments, giving you insight into how world-class players actually think through tough spots.

The Instructors: Elias and Petrangelo’s Credibility

Darren Elias brings unmatched WPT expertise and a teaching style that breaks down complex concepts into actionable strategies. His track record speaks for itself—four WPT titles is a feat that demonstrates consistency at the highest levels of tournament poker.

Nick Petrangelo, known in the poker community for his analytical approach and GTO-influenced play, adds a modern, solver-backed perspective to the curriculum. His ability to explain ICM pressure and final table dynamics is particularly valuable for players looking to improve their deep-run results.

The combination of Elias’s proven tournament success and Petrangelo’s technical expertise creates a well-rounded learning experience that addresses both fundamental strategy and cutting-edge concepts.

Key Strengths of Road to Victory

Comprehensive ICM Coverage: The course excels at teaching ICM (Independent Chip Model) concepts that are crucial for tournament success but often poorly understood by recreational players. The final table modules alone justify the course price for serious MTT grinders.

Real-World Application: Unlike purely theoretical courses, Road to Victory emphasizes practical application through actual hand histories from major tournaments. You see how these pros navigate the exact situations you’ll face at the tables.

Production Quality: Upswing Poker maintains high production standards throughout. The video quality, organization, and presentation make complex topics digestible, even during marathon study sessions.

Lifetime Access: Once purchased, you get lifetime access to all course materials, including any future updates. This means you can revisit concepts as your game evolves and benefit from new content additions.

Community Support: Access to the Upswing Poker Lab community allows you to discuss hands, share experiences, and network with other serious tournament players working through the same material.

Potential Drawbacks

Price Point: Road to Victory carries a premium price tag that may be prohibitive for casual players or those just starting their poker journey. While the content quality justifies the cost for serious players, it’s definitely an investment.

Advanced Concepts: Some modules assume a solid foundation in poker fundamentals. Complete beginners might struggle with certain sections without first building their baseline knowledge through more introductory resources.

Volume of Content: With 50+ hours of material, the course can feel overwhelming. Players need to commit significant time not just to watching videos but to implementing concepts at the tables.

Who Should Buy Road to Victory?

This course is ideal for:

  • Intermediate to advanced tournament players looking to sharpen their edge
  • Cash game players transitioning to tournaments
  • Players who regularly deep-run but struggle with final table dynamics
  • Serious MTT grinders willing to invest in their poker education
  • Players with at least a basic understanding of ICM and tournament theory

Not recommended for:

  • Complete poker beginners
  • Casual recreational players
  • Those exclusively focused on cash games
  • Players unwilling to dedicate substantial study time

Does Road to Victory Actually Improve Results?

The honest answer: it depends entirely on your commitment to implementation. The strategies taught by Elias and Petrangelo are proven at the highest levels of tournament poker. However, simply watching videos won’t transform your results—you need to actively study, take notes, and apply concepts at the tables.

Many students report noticeable improvements in their final table performance and decision-making under ICM pressure after completing the course. The edge gained from properly understanding tournament-specific concepts like bubble factors, effective stack sizes, and deal-making can directly impact your ROI in MTTs.

Road to Victory vs. Other Tournament Courses

Compared to alternatives like Jonathan Little’s tournament offerings or free YouTube content, Road to Victory provides more depth and modern, solver-informed strategies. While Jonathan Little’s courses offer excellent value, Road to Victory targets a slightly more advanced audience with its emphasis on high-level play.

Free content from YouTube and poker forums can supplement your learning but lacks the comprehensive, structured approach that Road to Victory provides. For players serious about tournament poker as a long-term pursuit, the investment in structured, professional instruction typically pays dividends.

The Verdict: Is Road to Victory Worth It?

Rating: 4.5/5 Stars

Road to Victory ranks among the best tournament poker training courses available today. The combination of world-class instruction from proven champions, comprehensive ICM coverage, and practical hand analysis makes it a valuable resource for serious tournament players.

The course delivers on its promise to provide elite-level tournament strategy, but it requires commitment. If you’re willing to put in the study hours and have the bankroll to justify the investment, Road to Victory can genuinely elevate your tournament game.

For intermediate players looking to break through to the next level or experienced grinders seeking to refine their final table play, this course represents excellent value despite the premium price point.

Final Recommendation

Buy Road to Victory if: You’re an intermediate or advanced player serious about tournament poker, you have the time to dedicate to proper study and implementation, and you’re looking to master ICM and final table dynamics.

Skip it if: You’re a complete beginner, you’re only casually interested in tournaments, or you’re not prepared to invest both the money and substantial study time required to extract maximum value.

For those committed to tournament poker mastery, Road to Victory provides the roadmap—you just need to put in the work to follow it.

content_html:
f you have been grinding No Limit Hold’em (NLHE) or PLO for years, you’ve likely noticed a trend: the edges are getting thinner. As the “Cadillac of Poker” becomes increasingly solved, many profitable players are looking for greener pastures.

Enter Mixed Games.

Whether it’s the dealer’s choice games in Vegas or the prestigious $50K Poker Players Championship, mixed games are where the wealthy amateurs still play for fun—and where the sharks are currently migrating.

Today, we are doing a deep dive into Upswing Poker’s “Mixed Games Mastery“, taught by high-stakes crusher Jake “JLlama” Abdalla. Is this $999 course the shortcut you need to dominate the mix, or is it an overpriced luxury? Let’s find out.

Who is Jake Abdalla?

Before dropping nearly a thousand dollars on a course, you need to know if the instructor is the real deal.

Jake Abdalla, known online as JLlama, is a legitimate end-boss in the mixed game world. Unlike some coaches who only theorize, Abdalla has millions in earnings and a reputation for beating the highest stakes online. He famously battled Phil Ivey heads-up and has successful results across almost every variant spread online.

The verdict on the instructor: You aren’t learning from a theorist; you are learning from a practitioner who has beaten the best in the world.

Course Overview: What Do You Get?

“Mixed Games Mastery” is not a general overview; it is a deep dive designed to take you from a NLHE player to a formidable mixed game opponent.

The course focuses on the five cornerstone variants found in most 8-Game or H.O.R.S.E. rotations:

  1. Razz
  2. Seven Card Stud
  3. Seven Card Stud Hi-Lo (Stud 8)
  4. Omaha Hi-Lo (Omaha 8)
  5. 2-7 Triple Draw

The Structure

Abdalla breaks down each game into specific modules. He assumes you understand basic poker concepts (pot odds, equity) but starts from the ground up for each specific variant.

  • The Basics: Rules, ante structures, and bring-in defense.
  • Street-by-Street Strategy: How to play 3rd street through 7th street (or draws in Triple Draw).
  • Heuristics & Ranges: Instead of memorizing thousands of charts, Abdalla teaches you how to construct ranges and estimate frequencies on the fly.

Key Features and Methodology

1. Ranges Over Rigid Charts

One of the SEO-friendly “golden nuggets” of this course is Abdalla’s teaching style. He knows you can’t memorize a solver chart for every Stud scenario. Instead, he focuses on heuristics (mental shortcuts) and range construction. He teaches you how to think about your opponent’s range relative to their up-cards or discard patterns.

2. The “Cross-Training” Approach

Abdalla often uses NLHE analogies to explain complex mixed game concepts. For example, he might compare a specific drawing situation in Triple Draw to a “polarized c-betting strategy” in Hold’em. This makes the content highly digestible for players transitioning from big-bet games.

3. “Perfect is the Enemy of Good”

A recurring theme in the course is practical playability. In mixed games, especially live, you don’t need to be GTO-perfect to win; you just need to be significantly better than the guy playing “bingo” in seat 4. The course focuses heavily on realizing your equity and avoiding catastrophic mistakes.

Pros and Cons

Every review needs an honest look at the good and the bad.

✅ The Pros

  • Elite Pedigree: Instruction from a confirmed high-stakes winner.
  • Comprehensive: It covers the most common mix variants in high detail.
  • Lifetime Access: Like all Upswing courses, you pay once and own it forever.
  • Mental Framework: It teaches you how to think like a mixed game player, which is more valuable than just being told what to play.
  • Triple Draw Section: Many users cite the 2-7 Triple Draw module as the “gold standard” of the course, worth the price of admission alone for draw game enthusiasts.

❌ The Cons

  • The Price: At $999, it is a significant investment.
  • Production Style: Some students have noted that the early videos can be a bit “lecture-heavy” with fewer hand examples than visual learners might prefer.
  • Minor Errors: There have been reports of minor errors in the “rules” sections (like tie-breaker explanations), though these don’t impact the high-level strategy.
  • Niche Audience: If you only play local $1/$2 NLHE, this course will not help you make money anytime soon.

Is “Mixed Games Mastery” Worth $999?

The $999 question. Here is the breakdown:

DO NOT BUY if:

  • You are a casual player who just wants to learn the rules of Stud for a $5 home game.
  • You are struggling to beat micro-stakes NLHE.
  • You are on a tight bankroll.

BUY IT IMMEDIATELY if:

  • You play live poker: Live mixed games (even at $4/$8 or $8/$16 limits) are often incredibly soft. One big pot won using Abdalla’s Triple Draw bluffing concepts could pay for the course.
  • You want to future-proof your career: As NLHE gets tougher, having a mixed-game edge is the ultimate insurance policy for a professional poker player.
  • You play online series (WCOOP/SCOOP): If you are tired of skipping the non-Hold’em events during major tournament series, this course will make you immediately competitive in those fields.

Final Verdict

Score: 4.5/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐✨

Upswing Poker’s Mixed Games Mastery is currently the best standalone library for serious players wanting to conquer non-Hold’em variants. While the price point is high, the lack of quality information elsewhere makes this a premium product with massive ROI potential. Jake Abdalla successfully demystifies complex games, turning “guessing” into “calculating.”

If you are ready to stop folding every hand in the Stud round and start crushing the rotation, this is the toolkit you need.

Next Step: Ready to expand your poker arsenal? Check out the Mixed Games Mastery course on Upswing Poker.

(Disclaimer: This review is for informational purposes. Always practice bankroll management when investing in training materials.)

title: Poker Math Every Player Needs to Know
excerpt: If you’ve been playing poker for any length of time, you’ve probably heard players throw around terms like pot odds, minimum defense frequency, and value-to-bluff ratios. These…
content_html:
If you’ve been playing poker for any length of time, you’ve probably heard players throw around terms like pot odds, minimum defense frequency, and value-to-bluff ratios. These concepts can seem overwhelming at first, like you need a mathematics degree just to compete at the tables.

Here’s the secret most poker coaches won’t tell you upfront: you don’t need to memorize five different formulas. In fact, all of poker’s essential math boils down to one single calculation applied in different situations.

The One Formula That Rules Them All

Every profitable decision in poker comes down to understanding your break-even point. Whether you’re deciding to call a bet, planning a bluff, or balancing your betting range, you’re really just asking the same question: “What needs to happen for this play to be profitable?”

The universal formula that answers this question is beautifully simple:

Break Even % = Risk ÷ (Risk + Reward)

That’s it. This one equation is the foundation of virtually every poker math concept you’ll encounter. Let me show you how it applies to the situations you face at the table every single session.

Understanding Risk and Reward

Before we dive into specific applications, let’s clarify what we mean by risk and reward:

Risk is what you stand to lose if your play doesn’t work out. When you’re calling a bet, it’s the amount you have to call. When you’re making a bluff, it’s the chips you’re putting into the pot.

Reward is what you gain when your play succeeds. This is typically the existing pot plus any bets that have been made.

Once you identify these two components in any poker situation, you can calculate exactly how often you need to be right for the play to be profitable.

Pot Odds: The Math of Calling

Pot odds are probably the first poker math concept most players learn, and they’re simply the risk-reward formula applied to calling decisions.

When your opponent bets, you need to figure out whether calling is profitable. Your risk is the amount you must call, and your reward is the total pot (everything already in the pot plus your opponent’s bet).

Let’s say there’s $75 in the pot and your opponent bets $25. You’re risking $25 to win $100 (the original $75 plus their $25 bet).

Using our formula: 25 ÷ (25 + 100) = 25 ÷ 125 = 20%

This means you need to have the best hand more than 20% of the time for calling to be profitable. If your hand equity is higher than 20%, calling makes money in the long run. If it’s lower, you should fold.

Value-to-Bluff Ratios: The Math of Balance

Here’s where poker math gets really interesting. Value-to-bluff ratios sound complicated, but they’re actually just pot odds viewed from the other side of the table.

The golden rule is this: On the river, your optimal bluffing frequency should equal the pot odds you’re offering your opponent.

If you bet half the pot, you’re giving your opponent 3:1 pot odds, which means they need 25% equity to call profitably. To keep them indifferent (unable to exploit you), your range should contain exactly 25% bluffs and 75% value hands.

This inverse relationship means that once you understand pot odds, you automatically understand optimal bluffing frequencies. They’re two sides of the same coin.

Alpha: The Math of Bluffing

“Alpha” is poker theory’s fancy name for something straightforward: the break-even success rate of your bluff.

When you’re considering a bluff, you’re risking your bet size to win the existing pot. Plug those numbers into our universal formula, and you get the exact percentage of time your opponent needs to fold for your bluff to show immediate profit.

For example, if you bet $60 into a $100 pot:

60 ÷ (60 + 100) = 60 ÷ 160 = 37.5%

Your opponent needs to fold more than 37.5% of the time for this bluff to be immediately profitable. If you believe they’ll fold 40% or 50% of the time, you’re printing money. If they’ll only fold 30% of the time, your bluff is losing money even before considering their equity when they call.

Minimum Defense Frequency: The Simpler Approach

Minimum Defense Frequency (MDF) tells you how often you need to defend against a bet to prevent your opponent from profitably over-bluffing you. Many players try to calculate this using its own complicated formula.

Don’t.

Instead, use this elegant shortcut: MDF = 1 minus Alpha.

When your opponent makes a bet, first calculate their Alpha (how often their bluff needs to work). If their bluff needs to succeed 60% of the time to break even, you must defend 40% of the time to keep them from profiting.

This relationship makes sense intuitively. If their bluff is profitable when you fold 60% of the time, you need to fold less than 60% to prevent them from exploiting you.

The “Easy Way” to Calculate Expected Value

Once you understand break-even percentages, there’s a powerful shortcut for calculating Expected Value that lets you quickly compare different lines of play.

EV = Edge × (Risk + Reward)

Your “edge” is the difference between the actual success rate and the break-even rate. If your opponent needs to fold 50% of the time for your bluff to break even, but they actually fold 60% of the time, you have a 10% edge.

Multiply that edge by the total pot (risk plus reward), and you get your expected value. If the pot is 5 big blinds and you have a 10% edge, your EV is 0.10 × 5 = 0.5 big blinds.

This method is especially useful when you’re reviewing hands and want to quickly determine whether calling or raising would have been more profitable.

The Gin and Tonic Analogy

If odds versus percentages still feel confusing, think about mixing a cocktail.

A Gin and Tonic recipe calls for 3 parts tonic water and 1 part gin. The ratio (odds) is 3:1, but the drink is 25% gin by volume (percentage). You get that 25% by dividing 1 part gin by 4 total parts.

In poker, if you must call 1 chip to win 3 chips, you’re looking at 3:1 pot odds. The total “drink” is 4 chips, and you need to provide the winning hand (the “gin”) 25% of the time to break even.

Why This Understanding Changes Everything

When you realize that pot odds, MDF, Alpha, and value-to-bluff ratios are all the same calculation in different disguises, poker math stops being about memorization and starts being about understanding incentives.

You begin to see the game as a series of interconnected decisions where knowing one thing automatically tells you several others. If you know the pot odds your opponent is getting, you know your optimal bluffing frequency. If you know the break-even success rate of a bluff, you know the correct defense frequency.

This unified understanding allows you to:

  • Make faster decisions at the table without pulling out calculators or fumbling through formulas
  • Spot opponents who are defending too much or too little against your bets
  • Recognize when you’re being exploited and adjust your strategy accordingly
  • Balance your ranges more intuitively because you understand the underlying math
  • Move from playing by rote to playing with genuine strategic comprehension

Putting It Into Practice

The next time you’re at the table and face a decision, try this simple process:

First, identify your risk and reward. What are you putting in versus what are you trying to win?

Second, calculate your break-even percentage using the universal formula.

Third, compare that percentage to either your equity (for calls) or your opponent’s likely folding frequency (for bluffs).

Finally, make your decision based on whether the actual frequency exceeds the break-even frequency.

With practice, these calculations become second nature. You’ll start to recognize common situations instantly: a half-pot bet requires 25% equity, a pot-sized bet requires 33%, a two-thirds pot bet requires 29%.

The Bottom Line

Poker math doesn’t have to be complicated. Despite what you might read in advanced strategy books or hear in coaching videos, you don’t need to master dozens of different formulas.

Master one formula, understand how risk and reward work in different contexts, and you’ll have the mathematical foundation to make profitable decisions in virtually any poker situation you encounter.

The pros who seem to have an instinctive feel for the right play? They’re not calculating complex equations in real-time. They’ve internalized this simple risk-reward relationship so thoroughly that correct play becomes automatic.

You can do the same. Start by consciously applying the break-even formula to your decisions, and over time, you’ll develop that same intuitive grasp of profitable poker math.

Unlike subscription-only platforms, BBZ Poker offers flexible options including individual courses, live seminars, personalized coaching, and a comprehensive video library with over 3,000 strategy videos.

The platform has built a strong reputation by coaching well-known professionals including Lex Veldhuis, Benjamin Spragg, and Fintan Hand. This poker training site focuses on practical, implementable strategies rather than pure theoretical solver outputs.

Serious Grinders: Individual courses provide focused training on specific leaks. The Simple Poker Systems bundle particularly offers exceptional ROI for players moving up stakes.

Who founded BBZ Poker? Jordan “bigbluffzinc” Drummond founded BBZ Poker in 2012. He’s a high-stakes professional with over 15 years in poker as a player, coach, and staker.

Final Verdict: BBZ Poker Review Rating

Rating: 4.5/5 Stars

BBZ Poker delivers professional-quality poker training with unmatched flexibility. The combination of extensive video content, interactive daily seminars, quality coaching, and supportive community creates an environment where dedicated players genuinely improve.

Jordan Drummond’s proven coaching credentials—having worked with top professionals—lend serious credibility to the educational approach. The platform’s emphasis on practical application over pure theory makes complex poker strategy accessible and implementable.

For serious players willing to invest time and money into poker education, BBZ Poker provides the tools, training, and support network needed for meaningful improvement. The platform’s track record of producing winning players through both direct coaching and the staking program demonstrates the effectiveness of their methodology.

content_html:
If you’re new to no-limit Texas hold’em, the learning curve can feel steep. Between understanding hand ranges, position play, bet sizing, and bankroll management, there’s a lot to absorb. Fortunately, the modern poker training landscape offers excellent resources designed specifically for beginners who want to build a solid foundation.

This guide breaks down the best poker training courses for newcomers to help you choose the right path for your poker education.

What Makes a Good Beginner Poker Course?

Before diving into specific recommendations, let’s establish what beginners should look for in a training course:

Clear fundamentals focus. The best beginner courses don’t overwhelm you with advanced game theory optimal play or complex solver outputs. Instead, they focus on core concepts like hand selection, position awareness, basic pot odds, and fundamental betting patterns.

Structured learning path. Random videos and scattered lessons won’t help you build knowledge systematically. Look for courses with a clear progression from absolute basics to intermediate concepts.

Interactive elements. Poker is learned by doing, not just watching. Courses with quizzes, hand history reviews, and practice scenarios help reinforce concepts much more effectively than passive video consumption.

Affordable pricing. As a beginner, you shouldn’t need to invest hundreds of dollars before knowing if poker is right for you. Many excellent courses offer free content or budget-friendly monthly subscriptions.

Top Poker Training Courses for Beginners

PokerCoaching.com (Free and Paid Tiers)

Jonathan Little’s PokerCoaching platform stands out for its beginner-friendly approach and generous free content. The site offers a structured “Poker Fundamentals” course that covers everything from basic hand rankings to position strategy and bet sizing fundamentals.

What makes PokerCoaching particularly valuable for beginners is the tiered approach. You can start with completely free lessons to see if the teaching style resonates with you, then upgrade to premium content as you progress. The paid membership includes weekly training videos, hand reviews, and access to a supportive community forum where you can ask questions.

The platform also features regular webinars and live training sessions, giving beginners the chance to learn in real-time and ask questions directly. Jonathan Little’s teaching style is clear and methodical, making complex concepts accessible without dumbing them down.

Upswing Poker Lab

The Upswing Poker Lab, created by Doug Polk and Ryan Fee, offers one of the most comprehensive structured curriculums available. While it includes advanced content, the “Core” section is specifically designed for beginners and low-stakes players.

The course uses a module-based approach, starting with preflop fundamentals and gradually building toward more complex postflop scenarios. Each module includes video lessons, quizzes to test your understanding, and practice exercises that help cement the concepts.

What distinguishes Upswing is the production quality and organization. The lessons feel more like a university course than random poker tips, with clear learning objectives and measurable progress tracking. The monthly membership model makes it affordable, and the sheer volume of content means you’ll have material to work through for months.

Red Chip Poker

Red Chip Poker targets the recreational player who wants to improve without becoming a full-time grinder. Their “Core” membership level is perfect for beginners, offering a logical progression through poker fundamentals.

The platform’s strength lies in its practical approach. Rather than overwhelming you with theory, Red Chip focuses on exploitative strategies that work well at low stakes where opponents make predictable mistakes. Their CORE workshops break down specific situations you’ll encounter regularly, like playing from the blinds or defending against continuation bets.

Red Chip also offers affordable poker training books that complement their video content, and their podcast provides free supplemental learning for those on a budget.

Run It Once (Essential Subscription)

Run It Once, founded by Phil Galfond, has built a reputation for high-quality poker instruction. While the platform includes advanced content for serious players, the Essential subscription tier offers excellent value for beginners.

The “From The Ground Up” series provides a comprehensive introduction to no-limit hold’em, covering everything from basic terminology to fundamental strategic concepts. The instructors on Run It Once are known for their ability to explain complex ideas clearly, making it easier for beginners to grasp important concepts without feeling lost.

One unique feature is the platform’s emphasis on thinking processes rather than memorization. Instead of telling you exactly what to do in every situation, instructors teach you how to analyze hands and make decisions based on sound reasoning.

BBZ Poker (Raise Your Edge)

While BBZ Poker and Raise Your Edge are often associated with advanced tournament play, their foundational content is surprisingly beginner-friendly. The courses emphasize understanding concepts rather than memorizing charts, which helps new players develop genuine poker intuition.

The platform offers a “Preflop Bootcamp” that’s invaluable for beginners struggling with hand selection and opening ranges. By mastering preflop play first, you’ll avoid many costly mistakes that plague new players.

The monthly subscription model is affordable, and the content is regularly updated to reflect current game conditions. BBZ’s teaching style is energetic and engaging, which helps maintain motivation during the sometimes-tedious process of learning fundamentals.

Free Resources Worth Exploring

Before committing to a paid course, consider exploring these free resources:

PokerStars School offers completely free courses covering basics through intermediate play, with interactive quizzes and a structured curriculum. While the content isn’t as deep as paid platforms, it’s an excellent starting point.

Splitsuit’s YouTube channel provides free videos on fundamental concepts, with clear explanations and practical examples. The content focuses on exploitative play at low stakes, making it immediately applicable for beginners.

r/poker subreddit and the TwoPlusTwo forums offer free hand analysis and strategy discussion. While not structured courses, these communities can provide valuable feedback on your play and answer specific questions.

Choosing the Right Course for You

The best poker training course depends on your learning style, budget, and goals:

If you prefer highly structured learning with clear progression, Upswing Poker Lab or Red Chip Poker are excellent choices. If you want to sample content before committing, start with PokerCoaching’s free tier. If you’re on a tight budget, explore free resources like PokerStars School before investing in paid training.

Most importantly, remember that poker education requires active engagement. Simply watching videos won’t improve your game. Take notes, review your own hands, participate in forums, and apply what you learn at the tables. The best course is the one you’ll actually complete and implement.

Final Thoughts

Learning no-limit hold’em is a journey, not a destination. The courses mentioned above provide solid foundations, but your real education happens at the tables where you apply these concepts. Start with fundamentals, be patient with your progress, and don’t rush into higher stakes before you’re ready.

Whichever course you choose, commit to the process. Study consistently, review your sessions, and focus on understanding concepts rather than memorizing solutions. With dedication and the right training resources, you’ll build the skills necessary to become a winning player.

title: The GTO Blueprint by Saulo Costa: A Comprehensive Course Review
excerpt: Introduction In the evolving landscape of online poker education, Game Theory Optimal (GTO) strategy has become essential for players looking to compete at mid-to-high stakes.…
content_html:
Introduction

In the evolving landscape of online poker education, Game Theory Optimal (GTO) strategy has become essential for players looking to compete at mid-to-high stakes. Saulo Costa’s “The GTO Blueprint” positions itself as a bridge course designed to transform low-stakes grinders into formidable mid-stakes regulars. But does it deliver on this ambitious promise? In this in-depth review, we’ll examine the course structure, content quality, target audience, and overall value proposition.

Who is Saulo Costa?

Saulo Costa, also known as “Metagame” in the online poker community, has built a reputation as both a successful cash game player and poker educator. His approach focuses on making complex GTO concepts accessible to players who want to implement solver-based strategies without getting lost in overwhelming theory.

Course Overview and Target Audience

The GTO Blueprint aims to transition players from low-stakes grinders to solid mid-stakes professionals, specifically targeting those who already have a foundational understanding of poker and are comfortable at stakes up to 100NL. The course explicitly states it’s recommended for players at 100nl+ who are already familiar with GTO.

Ideal Students:

  • Players moving from low stakes (NL50-NL100) to mid stakes (NL200+)
  • Cash game regulars seeking to develop unexploitable strategies
  • MTT players wanting to strengthen their technical fundamentals
  • Grinders who understand basic GTO but struggle with practical application

Not Recommended For:

  • Complete poker beginners
  • Players unfamiliar with GTO terminology
  • Those without solver experience
  • Recreational players at micro stakes

Course Structure and Content Breakdown

The GTO Blueprint is organized into eight comprehensive modules covering both theoretical foundations and practical applications across common game situations.

Module 1: Fundamental Aspects of Pseudo GTO Execution

The course opens with an accessible introduction to implementing GTO strategies in real-world scenarios. Rather than overwhelming students with pure solver outputs, Costa focuses on “pseudo GTO” execution—approximating optimal play using learnable heuristics and patterns that work at the tables without requiring perfect memorization.

Module 2: Pillars of GTO Strategy

This section tackles core strategic concepts including barreling strategies, slowplaying mechanics, bluff-catching principles, and bet-sizing theory. The emphasis on mixing strategies with draws and understanding balanced play gives students the tools to remain unpredictable against thinking opponents.

Module 3: Universal Heuristics for GTO Play

One of the course’s strongest sections, Module 3 presents actionable decision-making guidelines that apply across various situations. Topics include river bluffing and bluff-catching factors, block betting from out of position, and exploiting common tendencies while maintaining balance.

Modules 4-8: Advanced Strategy for SRP & 3-Bet Pots

The latter half of the course dives deep into specific game trees. These modules systematically cover:

  • Single-raised pots in position and out of position
  • Three-bet pot navigation as both aggressor and defender
  • Flop, turn, and river decision-making based on board textures
  • Delayed c-betting strategies
  • Responding to aggression in bloated pots

Key Strengths of The GTO Blueprint

Practical Heuristics Over Theory Overload

Unlike courses that drown students in solver screenshots and complex frequencies, Costa distills GTO principles into memorable heuristics. This approach allows players to make sound decisions at the tables without analysis paralysis.

Comprehensive Coverage of Common Situations

The extensive modules covering single-raised pots and three-bet pots—both in and out of position—address the vast majority of hands players will encounter. This practical focus ensures students can immediately apply lessons to their regular games.

Bridge Between Exploitative and Balanced Play

The course acknowledges that pure GTO isn’t always optimal against weak opponents but provides students with a solid baseline strategy that can’t be easily exploited by competent regulars. From this foundation, players can make targeted exploitative adjustments.

Pre-Recorded Content for Self-Paced Learning

All content is pre-recorded, allowing students to learn at their own pace, review difficult concepts, and reference specific modules as needed during their study sessions.

Potential Limitations

Prerequisites May Limit Accessibility

The course explicitly requires GTO familiarity and recommends it for 100NL+ players. Those hoping to learn GTO from scratch will need to start with introductory materials or Costa’s “Lowstakes Blueprint” course first.

No Live Coaching Component

While the pre-recorded format offers flexibility, students seeking personalized feedback or the ability to ask specific questions won’t find that here. The course is purely instructional without interactive elements.

Rapidly Evolving Game Environment

GTO solutions and solver outputs continue to evolve as poker theory advances. While fundamental principles remain sound, some specific strategic recommendations may require updates as the player pool adapts and solvers improve.

Value Proposition and Investment

Poker education represents an investment in your long-term win rate. By applying practical heuristics, the course promises to help players develop strategies that won’t be easily exploited, which translates directly to improved red-line performance and reduced losses to competent regulars.

For players serious about climbing stakes, the cost of a quality course often pales in comparison to the buy-ins lost through strategic leaks and exploitable play patterns. If The GTO Blueprint helps you plug even a few big blinds per 100 hands of leak, it can pay for itself within weeks at mid-stakes.

Comparison to Alternative GTO Resources

Versus Pure Solver Study

Self-studying with solvers like GTO+ or PioSolver offers unlimited customization but requires enormous time investment and can lead to information overload. Costa’s course provides curated, structured learning that’s more efficient for most players.

Versus Training Sites

Subscription sites like Run It Once or Upswing offer broader content libraries, but finding a coherent learning path can be challenging. The GTO Blueprint’s focused curriculum provides clear direction for mid-stakes preparation.

Versus Private Coaching

One-on-one coaching offers personalized attention but costs significantly more per hour of instruction. This course delivers professional-level insights at a fraction of coaching rates.

Final Verdict

The GTO Blueprint by Saulo Costa succeeds in its stated mission: providing low-stakes graduates with the theoretical framework and practical tools needed to compete at mid-stakes. The course strikes an effective balance between GTO theory and table-ready heuristics, making solver-based concepts accessible without overwhelming complexity.

Pros:

  • Practical, application-focused approach to GTO concepts
  • Comprehensive coverage of SRP and 3-bet pot scenarios
  • Clear progression from fundamentals to advanced strategy
  • Memorable heuristics that translate directly to table decisions
  • Self-paced pre-recorded format

Cons:

  • Requires existing GTO knowledge (not beginner-friendly)
  • No interactive coaching or personalized feedback
  • Limited to cash game applications (though concepts transfer to MTTs)
  • May need supplementary materials for complete solver fluency

Rating: 8.5/10

Recommendation: Highly recommended for serious cash game players at NL100-NL200 looking to solidify their theoretical foundation and reduce exploitability against competent regulars. The course delivers substantial value for players committed to mid-stakes success, though beginners should start with more foundational materials.

Whether you’re tired of getting pushed around by aggressive regs, struggling to know when to bluff or bluff-catch, or simply want to add theoretical rigor to your game, The GTO Blueprint provides a structured pathway to balanced, winning poker at mid-stakes and beyond.

Looking to elevate your game? Consider whether your current strategy stands up to competent opposition. If you’re regularly being exploited or unsure whether your decisions are theoretically sound, The GTO Blueprint might be the structured learning experience you need to reach the next level.

title: Why Every Poker Player Should Learn 5-Card PLO (And How to Start)
excerpt: If you’ve been grinding No-Limit Hold’em or even 4-Card PLO for years, you might be wondering whether it’s worth investing time into 5-Card Pot Limit Omaha. The short answer?…
content_html:
If you’ve been grinding No-Limit Hold’em or even 4-Card PLO for years, you might be wondering whether it’s worth investing time into 5-Card Pot Limit Omaha. The short answer? Absolutely. Five-card PLO represents one of the most exciting opportunities in modern poker, combining the action of traditional PLO with deeper strategic complexity that rewards skilled players.

The Game is Growing Fast

While No-Limit Hold’em remains poker’s most popular variant, 5-Card PLO has been quietly gaining traction in both online and live poker rooms. Major poker sites now spread regular games, and high-stakes pros have increasingly added it to their repertoire. This growth creates a window of opportunity: the player pool is still developing, meaning there’s significant edge available for those who invest in learning proper strategy now.

Why 5-Card PLO Offers Unique Advantages

The addition of just one extra card fundamentally transforms the game. In 5-Card PLO, hand equities run closer together preflop, which means the game becomes less about cards and more about skill. Post-flop play takes on entirely new dimensions, with more complex texture analysis, drawing dynamics, and hand reading requirements.

This complexity is actually a feature, not a bug. Games where skill matters more create better long-term earning potential for dedicated students of the game. While recreational players are drawn to the action and big pots, serious players can exploit the deeper strategic elements.

The Edge is Bigger Than You Think

Many players who transition from Hold’em or 4-Card PLO make fundamental mistakes in 5-Card PLO. They overvalue certain hand types, misread board textures, or fail to adjust their ranges properly. Because the game is newer and educational resources are still limited compared to Hold’em, the average skill level lags behind more established variants.

This creates an environment where proper study pays immediate dividends. Understanding concepts like hand coordination, nut advantage, and proper equity realization can put you miles ahead of opponents who are playing on intuition alone.

It Sharpens Your Overall Poker Skills

Learning 5-Card PLO doesn’t just make you a better Omaha player—it enhances your entire poker skill set. The game forces you to think in terms of ranges more precisely, improves your ability to calculate complex equities, and develops your hand reading abilities. The strategic thinking required translates directly back to other variants, making you a more well-rounded player overall.

Starting Your 5-Card PLO Journey

The biggest challenge with 5-Card PLO has been finding quality educational content. Unlike Hold’em, where countless resources exist, structured 5-Card PLO training has been harder to come by.

That’s where specialized courses come in. Run It Once offers “From The Ground Up: 5-Card PLO,” a comprehensive training program designed specifically for players looking to master this variant. The course takes you through everything from basic hand selection and preflop strategy to advanced post-flop concepts and population tendencies.

What makes structured learning valuable for 5-Card PLO is that the game’s complexity means trial-and-error learning is expensive. Investing in proper education upfront saves you from costly mistakes at the table and accelerates your learning curve dramatically.

The Time to Learn is Now

The poker landscape is always evolving, and early adopters of emerging variants consistently find themselves with an edge. Five-card PLO is past the experimental phase but hasn’t yet reached the saturation point where games become tougher across the board.

Whether you’re a professional looking to diversify your game selection, a recreational player seeking new challenges, or someone who’s hit a plateau in other variants, 5-Card PLO offers fresh strategic territory to explore. The combination of growing game availability, a developing player pool, and the pure enjoyment of navigating complex poker situations makes it an ideal time to add this variant to your repertoire.

The players who dedicate themselves to learning 5-Card PLO now will be the ones reaping the rewards as the game continues to grow. Don’t wait until everyone else has caught up—start building your edge today.

When it comes to multi-table tournament (MTT) poker training, finding a course that systematically builds your skills from fundamentals to advanced strategy can be challenging. Run It Once’s “From The Ground Up MTT Edition” promises to do exactly that, offering a structured approach to tournament poker education. In this comprehensive review, we’ll explore whether this course delivers on its promise and who can benefit most from it.

What Is From The Ground Up MTT Edition?

From The Ground Up MTT Edition is a poker training course developed by Run It Once, one of the industry’s most respected poker training platforms. The course is designed to take players through a progressive learning journey, starting with fundamental MTT concepts and advancing through increasingly complex tournament situations and strategies.

Course Structure and Content

The strength of this course lies in its methodical approach to tournament poker education. Rather than jumping between disconnected concepts, From The Ground Up MTT Edition builds each lesson upon the previous one, creating a cohesive learning experience that mirrors how successful tournament players actually develop their skills.

The curriculum covers essential MTT topics including:

Early Game Strategy – Understanding how to build a stack when blinds are low and stacks are deep, including opening ranges, three-betting strategies, and early-game hand selection.

Mid-Game Adjustments – Navigating the crucial middle stages where many players struggle, covering stack-size dependent strategies and bubble dynamics.

Late Game and Final Table Play – Advanced concepts for deep tournament runs, including ICM considerations, short-stack play, and exploitative adjustments against different opponent types.

Tournament-Specific Situations – Detailed analysis of unique MTT scenarios such as satellite strategy, dealing with antes, and adjusting to different tournament structures.

Teaching Methodology

What sets this course apart from random YouTube videos or forum posts is its systematic teaching approach. The instructors break down complex concepts into digestible segments, using real-world examples from actual tournament hands to illustrate key principles. This combination of theory and practical application helps students understand not just what to do, but why certain plays are optimal in tournament contexts.

The course uses a variety of teaching tools including hand history reviews, theoretical explanations, and strategic frameworks that players can apply at the tables immediately.

Who Should Take This Course?

Beginners to Intermediate Players – If you’re new to tournament poker or have been playing recreationally without consistent results, this course provides the structured foundation you need. The “from the ground up” approach ensures you won’t have knowledge gaps in your game.

Cash Game Players Transitioning to Tournaments – Cash game specialists often struggle with tournament-specific concepts like ICM, bubble play, and stack-size adjustments. This course addresses these unique MTT elements comprehensively.

Self-Taught Players Looking to Formalize Their Knowledge – If you’ve learned through trial and error or scattered resources, this course can help organize your knowledge and fill in strategic blind spots.

Pros and Cons

Advantages:

  • Systematic progression from basic to advanced concepts
  • High-quality instruction from experienced tournament professionals
  • Tournament-specific focus rather than generic poker advice
  • Practical application through real hand examples
  • Access to Run It Once’s broader community and resources

Potential Drawbacks:

  • Requires time commitment to work through the full curriculum
  • May cover some basic concepts that experienced players already know

Is From The Ground Up MTT Edition Worth It?

For serious players looking to improve their tournament results, From The Ground Up MTT Edition represents a solid investment in poker education. The structured approach eliminates the inefficiency of piecing together strategy from various sources, while the quality of instruction ensures you’re learning proven, theoretically sound concepts.

The course is particularly valuable for players who learn best through systematic, organized content rather than random strategy articles. While experienced tournament grinders might find some sections review material, the comprehensive nature ensures even skilled players will discover new concepts or refine their existing knowledge.

Final Verdict

From The Ground Up MTT Edition successfully delivers on its promise of providing comprehensive, structured tournament poker education. Run It Once has established itself as a premier training site for good reason, and this course exemplifies their commitment to quality instruction.

For players serious about improving their MTT results and willing to invest time in structured learning, this course offers excellent value. The combination of fundamental coverage, advanced strategy, and practical application creates a learning experience that can genuinely transform your tournament game.

Whether you’re looking to take your hobby play to the next level or building skills for professional tournament poker, From The Ground Up MTT Edition provides the educational foundation you need to compete successfully in today’s competitive MTT landscape.

title: How to Study Poker Like a Pro With Uri Peleg
excerpt: Learning how to study poker effectively separates winning players from the rest. While most recreational players review hands to see if they made mistakes, professional players…
content_html:
Learning how to study poker effectively separates winning players from the rest. While most recreational players review hands to see if they made mistakes, professional players like Uri Peleg approach poker study with a completely different mindset—one focused on building a comprehensive knowledge base rather than validating individual decisions.

The Professional Mindset: Think Like a Chess Player

The biggest shift you need to make is moving from hand-by-hand analysis to strategic thinking. Uri Peleg uses a powerful analogy: think of poker like a chessboard.

When a recreational player looks at a hand like Queen-Jack of spades, they’re typically wondering, “Did I play this specific hand correctly?” But when a professional analyzes the same situation, they’re asking, “What should I be doing in this spot with my entire range?”

This distinction is crucial. Pros don’t study poker to validate whether they won or lost a particular hand. Instead, their goal is to add to their Expected Value (EV) and build a knowledge base they can apply across countless similar situations. By learning concepts that work across the board, you naturally improve your overall win rate.

Understanding Stack-to-Pot Ratio (SPR) Context

One of the most important aspects of professional poker study is understanding how strategy shifts based on Stack-to-Pot Ratio (SPR). This concept determines which hands you should play aggressively and which require caution.

Shallow SPR Strategy

When playing with a shallow SPR (less money behind relative to the pot), draw values change dramatically. Strong draws to the nuts actually become devalued because there’s less money to win when you hit.

In shallow SPR situations, hands like open-ended straight draws (Queen-Jack) should often bet once rather than trying to build a larger pot over multiple streets. The goal is to keep money behind so you can extract maximum value when your draw completes. You’re not in a rush to get all the money in.

Interestingly, in shallow SPR spots, you might even prefer weaker draws like Ace-Jack (drawing to top pair) because at shallow stack depths, top pair “does a job”—it’s strong enough to win the pot.

Deep SPR Strategy

When stacks are deep (300 big blinds or more, or in single-raised pots), the entire dynamic flips. Open-ended straight draws often start checking instead of betting because you want to build larger pots with your premium holdings. In deep-stacked situations, you need stronger hands to commit significant portions of your stack.

Why SPR Context Matters

Understanding these SPR-based adjustments is essential because game conditions constantly change. Sometimes you’re facing a short stack, other times a deep stack. Sometimes it’s a four-bet pot, other times a three-bet pot. The amount of money behind determines which hands you should use for check-raise bluffs and which hands should simply bet.

Mastering Range Composition and Give-Up Frequency

When Uri Peleg studies poker, he pays close attention to range composition—particularly on the river after draws have missed.

The Necessity of Giving Up

If you check-raised earlier in the hand with a range containing both value hands and draws, and all your draws miss by the river, you’re required to give up with a significant portion of your range. This isn’t optional—it’s mathematically necessary.

For instance, if you’re holding hands with no showdown value or just King-high, you often need to give up 75% of the time. There must be a give-up frequency with your air, especially when you don’t have busted flush draws to use as your primary bluffing candidates.

Avoiding the Over-Bluffing Trap

Many players fall into the trap of thinking every missed draw looks like a good bluff. Hands like Queen-Jack, King-Jack, 8-6, and 7-6 might all seem like justifiable river bluffs, but in reality, you need to give up with most of them.

As a general rule, Queen-Jack offsuit should never bluff in many river situations, while Queen-Jack suited might be used as a mixed strategy bluff. Understanding these subtle differences separates break-even players from consistent winners.

Advanced Concepts for Serious Students

For players already competing at mid-to-high stakes, Uri Peleg explores even more nuanced concepts.

Implementing Realistic GTO Models

When using solvers like GTO Wizard, professionals don’t just accept the default outputs. They often edit the model to reflect more realistic gameplay. For example, you might reduce three suggested bet sizes down to one polar size that better represents how you actually play.

Blocking Effects and Card Removal

Does blocking certain combinations (like blocking trips with spades) matter for your bluffing frequencies? While you might expect suited hands to perform better because they block opponent trip combinations, solvers often manipulate ranges to create suit indifference—meaning your specific suit doesn’t significantly change your bluffing frequency in that context.

However, against naive opponents who don’t employ complex mixed strategies, blocking trips absolutely matters. These advanced suit manipulation concepts are most relevant at nosebleed stakes and shouldn’t be a priority unless you’re already playing at the highest levels.

The Meteorologist Approach to Poker Study

Uri Peleg’s approach to studying poker is like becoming a meteorologist. You’re not trying to explain why it rained yesterday—you’re trying to understand the complex systems (SPR dynamics, range composition, game theory equilibrium) that govern outcomes so you can predict and adapt to any future scenario.

This systematic approach to poker study means:

  • Analyzing entire ranges, not individual hands
  • Understanding how SPR changes your strategic approach
  • Learning appropriate give-up frequencies to avoid over-bluffing
  • Building a knowledge base you can apply to countless situations
  • Focusing on concepts that increase your overall win rate

Start Studying Like a Pro Today

The difference between recreational and professional poker study isn’t about how many hours you put in—it’s about what you’re studying and why. By adopting Uri Peleg’s professional mindset, you’ll transform your game from reactive decision-making to strategic mastery.

Stop asking “Did I play this hand right?” and start asking “What’s the optimal strategy for my entire range in this situation?” That single shift in perspective will accelerate your poker improvement more than any other change you can make.

Remember: every study session should add to your knowledge base and increase your EV across multiple situations. Think in ranges, contextualize with SPR, master your frequencies, and approach each concept like a system to understand rather than a hand to judge.

That’s how you study poker like a pro.

Final Verdict: Should You Buy Advanced PLO Mastery?

Rating: 4.5/5 Stars
